In ACC After Dark action, Stanford hosts NC State at Stanford Stadium in Stanford, Calif., on Friday at 10:30 p.m. ET (ESPN). The Wolfpack are 6.5-point road favorites, and my NC State vs. Stanford prediction and college football picks expect CJ Bailey to pick apart one of the Power Four's worst defenses. TOP PICK Who will win NC State vs Stanford: NC State -6.5 Stanford has been completely uncompetitive in four of its last five FBS games and is 1-5 ATS since the start of September. While NC State isn't a powerhouse, the Wolfpack have enough offense to cover up to -8.5 on the road . The Cardinal have lost four of their last five FBS games by at least 28 points and scored seven or fewer in all four (they were outscored 115-10 in their last two FBS games) . With a defense that's ranked 127th in success rate (50.1%) , Stanford's offense won't be able to keep up with the Wolfpack. NC State has scored 31+ points in three of its last four FBS games, all against defenses ranked higher by SP+ than Stanford's (111th). Plus, the Wolfpack are coming off a bye week and should be well rested for the West Coast trip. NC State vs Stanford Over/Under pick: Over 55.5 NC State and Stanford have struggling defenses, which have helped them consistently hit the Over this season. The Wolfpack and Cardinal are a combined 9-4 to the Over, and I like it to hit at 55.5 or better . Stanford's defense has the lowest havoc rate in the ACC (11.3%) and is allowing the second-most yards per game in the Power Four (452) . NC State's defense isn't all that much better, though, ranking 124th in net EPA per play and 133rd in EPA per pass. These two defenses bend and break, ranking the worst in the conference in points per opportunity on defense, though Stanford (5.06) is significantly worse than NC State (3.94). NC State vs Stanford combo Stanford is one of the worst teams in college football, and it doesn't look like Andrew Luck and Tavita Pritchard will be turning things around anytime soon. Though Davis Warren has been efficient at QB, the Cardinal have a dreadful defense that ranks outside the top 115 in EPA per pass, EPA per rush, and available yards percentage (57.3%). Even against an NC State defense giving up 27.7 points per game, Stanford won't be able to keep this close at home against David Doeren's team. The Wolfpack's passing game will be too much, and I have NC State winning 33-24 . away.blurb: But the program needs to get by without some key players. Ahead of the matchup, the ACC released official injury reports for this week. Stanford has multiple players still listed out, including linebacker Matt Rose and defensive back Brandon Nicholson. He has played at an elite level when healthy, but it is still to be disclosed how long he will be out. Stanford needs him back desperately to improve linebacker depth and production. Rose is the leader of the defense, and his presence elevates everyone around him. He's set to miss a significant amount of time, and it is highly possible that he will not return this season, putting the program in a tough spot. After Collin Wright missed time with an injury of his own last season, Nicholson shined and proved himself as a key player for the defense. Defensive backs Lonnie McAllister III and Chris Garland are questionable, while Lasiah Jackson is probable. NC State will be down some key stars as well. Running back Jayden Scott, defensive back Tristan Teasdell and tight end Vander Ploog headline the list of injured NC State players. Scott, NC State's leading rusher, has 62 carries for 358 yards and four touchdowns this season. With him out, it will be interesting to see how the Wolfpack's offense attacks. Wide receiver Jojo Trader and offensive tackle Kamen Smith are listed as questionable for the Wolfpack. If they return, they will provide a big boost. This game is big for both teams. For Stanford, a win puts them back at .500 and digs them out of a massive hole when it comes to returning to a bowl game. They would reach four wins, which is their total from last season, and would have a path to reaching a bowl game. That path evaporates with a loss. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings No. 6 Indiana looks to rebound from a loss to Ohio State, while Michigan begins again at quarterback Getty Images The Tommy Carr era in Ann Arbor will officially get underway this Saturday when the freshman quarterback makes his first career start at home against No. 6 Indiana . Carr led a second-half comeback last week against Penn State after former five-star recruit Bryce Underwood was benched, and Michigan made the decision to fully turn the operation over to Carr against an extremely good Indiana defense. That will present a major challenge for Carr, but it also shows Michigan's faith in him as the best option against the defending champs. Indiana comes into the game trying to shake off the frustration of a loss at home to Ohio State last week, coming a literal foot away from a win had Nick Marsh been able to keep his feet in bounds on a wide-open fourth-down pass from Josh Hoover . The Hoosiers need to refocus after the disappointment of their first loss in two years, as they head into the Big House to face a Michigan team that may not be elite on offense but will still present a stiff test for an Indiana offense that's been out of sync recently. The Hoosiers are 7.5-point road favorites, but the Wolverines suddenly have a bit of life after last week's win, and the excitement for a new quarterback will create a lively atmosphere in Ann Arbor. Michigan vs. Indiana: Need to know Tommy Carr's first start: Carr took over for Bryce Underwood at halftime against Penn State and performed solidly, leading three Michigan touchdown drives -- that came off three Penn State turnovers. While he only threw for 47 yards, playing complementary football and cashing in on great defensive plays to turn them into points is a major step forward for this Michigan offense. However, doing that against a bad Penn State team is one thing; now Carr will face an Indiana defense that's among the best in the country. He'll be tasked with not turning the ball over and taking what's in front of him, but Indiana will know that as well, and Michigan might have to let Carr turn it loose a couple of times down the field if they're going to force the Hoosiers off the line of scrimmage. Michigan knows this will be an extremely difficult first start for Carr and will likely try to protect him with quick concepts and a run-heavy approach, but if they want to pull off the upset, Carr is going to have to deliver a couple big plays Indiana's not expecting. Can Indiana establish a rhythm?: A stop-start offense has been a problem all season for Indiana, and while they escaped the first six games without it costing them, it finally caught up in Columbus. Now they face a Michigan defense that is also excellent and will present plenty of challenges, and Josh Hoover will have to prove he can move the ball consistently through the air. Indiana's offense has been predicated much more on the big play than they'd like this season, as Hoover has been able to create explosives in the passing game to Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh. However, consistency has been lacking, and that's kept the Hoosiers from pulling away from opponents as they did a year ago. Against Ohio State, Hoover threw for 296 yards, but completed just 20 of 40 passes to do so. He will need to figure out how to be sharper in the underneath and intermediate passing game if Indiana's going to have a chance of repeating, and that starts this week given the challenge Michigan will present up front. Elite run defenses: The Hoosiers and Wolverines are two of the nation's best defenses against the run, and that presents real problems for offenses that want to lean on their rushing attacks. Indiana struggled to get anything going against Ohio State, even with Turbo Richard back in the lineup, and they'll be up against it again with a Michigan defense that allows a paltry 2.68 yards per carry. One of the six teams better than Michigan against the run is Indiana, allowing just 2.28 yards per carry, which will put even more pressure on Carr to produce through the air in his first start. The team that can establish some kind of ground game will gain an advantage in this one, but there's a real possibility that neither can break through the walls of these defensive fronts. Where to watch Michigan vs. Indiana live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Michigan Stadium -- Ann Arbor, Michigan TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Michigan vs. Indiana prediction, picks We've got two elite run defenses, one inconsistent passing attack and one freshman making his first start. That is a recipe for a low-scoring battle. Michigan has played five games against teams not named UTEP , and all five games have finished with fewer than 40 points. Indiana's last two games have finished in the 30s as well, as they've faced the two best defenses on their schedule thus far, and it's hard to see a game flow here leading to anything approaching a shootout. The fear here is the potential for defensive scores, but even so, give me the under in Ann Arbor for the second straight week. picks.headline: 3 bold predictions for Indiana football vs. Michigan: Josh Hoover will have a day
picks.blurb: Indiana (6-1, 3-1 Big Ten), for the first time in a long time, is looking to get back on track. It’ll have an opportunity to do just that at Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) after falling last week to Ohio State at home. Can the Hoosiers do it ? That would be a hard yes if two of these bold predictions come true and one doesn’t. 3 bold predictions for Indiana at Michigan Michigan doesn’t score a touchdown The Wolverines, despite their abysmal offense through the first half of the season, have scored at least two touchdowns in every Big Ten game thus far. Expect that streak to be snapped by Indiana. The Hoosiers are simply a different test than anything Michigan has seen. True freshman Tommy Carr is poised to get his first career start on Saturday. And while it may be the best decision for the Wolverines, it couldn’t come against a tougher opponent. Indiana is going to speed Carr up, force Michigan to rely on its ground attack and then bottle that up (currently surrendering a Big Ten-best 2.3 yards per carry and just 75.4 total yards per game). The Wolverines might be able to trek into Hoosiers territory on occasion, but never into the end zone. The Hoosiers don’t crack 100 yards on the ground A few signs point in the right direction for Indiana’s run game on Saturday (at least from a total-yardage perspective). First of all, the Hoosiers run the ball a lot – and they’ve been very good at it in the Curt Cignetti era. In Indiana’s first two Big Ten outings, it registered 271 yards and 329 yards on the ground, respectively. Also, against Michigan, the expectation is that the Hoosiers should be leading most of the game. And there is no better way to nurse a lead than run the football. On the flip side, though, Indiana has managed a combined 138 rushing yards on 51 carries over the past two games. The offensive line has failed to get any push and the running backs haven’t been able to find any holes. Chunk plays, explosive plays – the Hoosiers can’t get anything positive (didn’t even have a single rush over 10 yards against Ohio State). The other bad news: Michigan’s rushing defense is elite. It allows just 2.7 yards per carry and 89.7 yards per game. This, unfortunately for Indiana, is a stoppable-force-meets-immovable-object scenario. Josh Hoover throws for three touchdowns Save for the Rutgers win – which, should that even count as Big Ten play? – quarterback Josh Hoover hasn’t thrown for three touchdowns in a league game. That may be set to change on Saturday, though. Michigan’s defense is flat-out dominant. But its lone vulnerability is defending the pass. Iowa’s Hank Brown threw for 227 yards and two scores. Penn State’s Rocco Becht slung it for 267 yards and a touchdown through the air. And, all due respect to both of those gunslingers, but neither is at the same level as Hoover, nor do they have the unreal weapons Hoover has on the outside. Expect Hoover and his stud wide receiver duo of Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh to feast against Michigan, especially considering the ongoing rushing struggles for the Hoosiers’ offense. Indiana will lead by three scores at half Unfortunately, I just don't think this Michigan team has what it takes this year to hang with Indiana because of the Hoosiers' defense. There is certainly some new hope with Carr in at quarterback, and it will be exciting to see his first start, but it is a very tall task for a freshman going up against one of the best defenses in the country. At the end of the day, this Indiana defense will just be too good. I still think Michigan's offense is heading in the right direction after the quarterback change, but this is a difficult matchup for even the most elite offenses in college football. away.headline: Ohio State vs. Indiana football injury report: Who’s in, who’s out for ranked Big Ten matchup
away.blurb: COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State freshman receiver Brock Boyd will be a game-time decisions for Saturday’s game at Indiana, according to the Big Ten’s final availability report. Boyd was deemed questionable on the first two injury reports of the week. He was downgraded to doubtful Friday. The Buckeyes will be without starting offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who did not play against Maryland last week and was listed as out throughout this week. Safety Leroy Roker and running back Ja’Kobi Jackson are also out. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, offensive lineman Phillip Daniels, defensive back Jay Timmons and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the injury report, meaning they’re available to play. Ohio State will have a crucial core of players who missed last week’s game back, though. The Buckeyes have been without Daniels, their starting right tackle, since he suffered an injury late in Ohio State’s Sept. 12 loss at Texas. In his absence, Siereveld moved from right guard to right tackle and Gabe VanSickle started at right guard. VanSickle moved to right tackle with Daniels and Siereveld sidelined last week. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said VanSickle will go back to right guard with Daniels reentering the lineup at right tackle. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.blurb: The Ohio State Buckeyes didn't play well offensively in Week 7 against the Indiana Hoosiers. Still, Ohio State football squeaked out of Bloomington , Indiana, with a 19-15 win. The bigger story coming out of the game is the status of quarterback Julian Sayin, who exited in the fourth quarter with an injury. “You know, I don't have a ton of details but he'll probably be out for several weeks,” Day stated . “So, you know, we'll have to come up with a plan there.” Coming out of the bye, Ohio State travels to face USC in Week 9 in another game the Buckeyes need to win. The Trojans are 6-1 and a top-20 team in the country. From there, Ohio State takes on Oregon in Week 10, another tough matchup. Meanwhile, Ohio State fans have to hold their breath on how long Sayin will be out, and exactly how long several weeks turns out to be. The bye week should bring more clarity and comes at a key time for the Buckeyes. home.headline: Michigan injury updates: Rod Moore ‘OK’ after being carted off in win
home.blurb: The Wolverines were down a second starting offensive lineman, guard Brady Norton, while center Jake Guarnera and guard Nathan Efobi both played through injuries in Saturday’s 21-18 victory at Michigan Stadium . Guarnera especially, having been listed as a game-time decision two hours before kickoff. “Everyone has something going on at this point in the season,” starting tackle Blake Frazier said. “I’m super proud of him. He was straining all week to make sure that he was giving himself the best opportunity to be out there with us today.” ANN ARBOR, Mich. — Michigan football continues to limp its way through the schedule, and the win over Penn State was no different. Michigan (4-2, 1-2 Big Ten) started backup Avery Gach at right guard while welcoming sixth offensive lineman Manuel Beigel back to the lineup. The Wolverines were able to run for a season-high 211 yards and three touchdowns, much of that coming in the second half with backup Tommy Carr at quarterback. In-game, though, the Wolverines had to deal with a couple of scares. Safety Rod Moore had to be carted off the field in the third quarter after intercepting a Rocco Becht pass; his first turnover of the season. “Should be OK,” Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham said. “It’s nothing major. Now, will he be ready for the next game? That’s debatable, but it’s nothing that’s long term.” That’s good news for Moore, who returned in full this season following a two-year rehab from a torn ACL and meniscus in his knee. He’s started all six games this season and is one of two captains on defense. Meanwhile, cornerback Jyaire Hill was missing in the secondary toward the end of the game, and Whittingham suggested an injury kept him from playing. “But it doesn’t appear to be anything — kind of like Rod — long term,” Whittingham said. Hill struggled in coverage against Penn State receiver Chase Sowell, who caught 11 passes for 151 yards and a touchdown and drew a pair of holding penalties against the senior defensive back. “That receiver is a good receiver,” Whittingham said. “A big, physical kid. I thought we were a little soft in pass defense this game. We needed to get up and challenge a little more, get in the receiver’s face and be a little bit more aggressive in that respect.” To illustrate how beaten up Michigan is, Whittingham said as many as six starters would have been sidelined last week had the Wolverines played a game. They were on a bye instead, giving the team enough time to get some players back in time. “It was good to get those guys healthy and be able to get them to this game and perform,” Whittingham said. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Getty Images One week after stunning No. 1 Georgia , Auburn will try to replicate that effort against No. 18 LSU . Auburn will have the Jordan-Hare Stadium crowd on it side, but the team faces an uphill battle in the pursuit of two major upsets. Going into its open date, Auburn was coming off a loss to Tennessee and needed something to build upon. An upset of the No. 1 team in the country on the road will certainly suffice, and now Alex Golesh must find a way to sustain that momentum. If Auburn is going to give itself a shot to slay SEC dragons in consecutive weeks, it will need to put the game on the shoulders of Byrum Brown again. He totaled 265 yards and a pair of touchdowns against the Bulldogs. On the other hand, LSU will have to be wary of entering a hostile environment given its recent history. The team has lost both of its road games this season, and Lane Kiffin's struggles away from home date back to when he first accepted the Ole Miss job. The Baton Rouge-based Tigers just shut out a shorthanded Mississippi State team in Death Valley, and Sam Leavitt played the first clean game of his LSU tenure. He'll need to replicate that performance in Auburn. Before this battle of the Tigers begins, we have everything you need to know about the matchup. LSU vs. Auburn: Need to know LSU's road woes: LSU is the clear favorite in this game, but it has struggled to win road games lately. The Tigers have dropped eight straight road games, which is the third-longest streak in school history. LSU is 0-2 on the road this fall, and Kiffin hasn't fared well away from home throughout his SEC coaching career. Between stops at Tennessee, Ole Miss and LSU, Kiffin is 14-16. Winning on the road is hard, but LSU can't make it even harder. Run, Bryum, run: If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense. That worked last week in Athens, as Brown toted the rock on 26 attempts, which included five sacks. The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs. Auburn trying to go back-to-back: Can Auburn pull off two stunners in a row? The Tigers haven't picked up wins over ranked teams in consecutive weeks since they rattled off three straight against Georgia, Alabama and Missouri in 2013. The trouble is that Auburn hasn't played well at home against ranked opponents of late, which is somewhat surprising given the general mystique around Jordan-Hare Stadium. The team is 1-9 in its last 10 home games against top-25 teams. Where to watch LSU vs. Auburn live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 12 p.m. ET Location : Jordan-Hare Stadium -- Auburn, Alabama TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free) LSU vs. Auburn prediction, picks What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable. Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double-digits. picks.blurb: LSU vs. Auburn Score Predictions: Who Wins and Why? Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB The No. 20 LSU Tigers will hit the road to face the Auburn Tigers on Saturday. LSU is coming off a dominant win over Mississippi State, while Auburn upset Georgia last week. LSU has looked like two different teams at home and on the road. At Tiger Stadium, LSU is 5-0 with an average margin of victory of 36.2. On the road, the Tigers are 0-2 and have allowed 67 points. The LSU on SI staff made their picks for this week's big matchup. LSU defensive tackle Deuce Geralds celebrates. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Brooke Benedict Brooke Benedict I think LSU will be able to get a road win on its record against Auburn, as the team will come off major momentum from the Georgia upset next year and let details and mistakes slip that LSU will pick up on and be able to dominate in. LSU’s defense is also coming off serious momentum after shutting out No. 16-ranked Mississippi State last week, a defensive influence that will be a key factor in the game against the unranked Auburn Tigers. Auburn has the home-field advantage, which has been a major weakness for LSU so far this season. That’s what makes the stakes so much higher for LSU this weekend, an expectation that they will be able to meet. LSU 31, Auburn 20 LSU returns star TE Trey'Dez Green after weeks of an injury-induced absence, and the Tigers in purple and gold have their backs against the wall. As much as they control their own destiny, a third loss on the road would almost certainly eliminate them from playoff contention. Auburn is also coming off a huge win over Georgia on the road, and I don't believe that Goleshs' squad is ready for another physical battle like LSU will bring. I think LSU's defense, especially DJ Pickett and Ty Benefield, will disrupt Byrum Brown enough for Sam Leavitt and the offense to put their foot on the gas. LSU 34, Auburn 21 Zion Trammell It appears LSU's offense is getting a massive boost, as Trey'Dez Green is set to return after a multi-week absence. However, I think LSU will lean on Dilin Jones to control time of possession and grab an early lead. Defensively, LSU has to make Auburn a one-dimensional offense and keep Byrum Brown in the pocket. If they can accomplish that, I think LSU gets a big road win. LSU 31, Auburn 17 Louisiana State Tigers running back Dilin Jones. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JD Andress Auburn is coming off a massive win, and the Tigers continue to battle injuries, but the way Sam Leavitt has been playing lately makes it hard to pick against LSU. He's found a rhythm as a pure pocket passer, and for the first time this season, didn't throw an interception last week. He should continue to play at a high level, and when he does, LSU wins because of it. Adrian Martinez LSU will look to carry the momentum from its dominant shutout win over Mississippi State into a tough battle at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Even though Auburn is coming off the upset of Georgia, I expect the LSU to be up to challenge and the Tigers defense to be flying around the field, keeping Auburn in check. If LSU can protect the football and avoid the mistakes that have hurt them on the road this season, I think they come away with a much-needed SEC road victory. LSU 28, Auburn 13 LSU will prove that the struggles on the road shouldn't be a concern. The offense will start fast, like it's shown it can do consistently and the defense will be stifling from the jump. LSU will get out to that hot start, and only accelerate, extending the streak of scoring over 30 points. The LSU Tigers bring the country's best opponent-adjusted net EPA profile to Jordan-Hare Stadium, while the Auburn Tigers still need Byrum Brown to manufacture too much of the offense himself. I'm laying the points with LSU and grabbing the Under as my best bet in this Tigers vs Tigers affair. Head over to our latest college football picks for more Week 8 betting analysis. Who will win LSU vs Auburn: LSU -7.5 I would play the LSU Tigers to 50%. Last week's win over the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs absolutely raises the Auburn Tigers ' ceiling, but it took 26 Byrum Brown carries and three Gunner Stockton turnovers to pull it off. Additionally, Auburn is coming off one of its biggest wins in recent memory. I'm not here to tell you that LSU is a better football team than Georgia, but its profile may be more suitable for this matchup. The visitors sit No. 1 nationally in opponent-adjusted net EPA per play at +0.44 , while Auburn is 35th at +0.14. Brown is Auburn's engine on the ground, yet he ranks 100th among qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's a dangerous imbalance against a defense that can crowd the box and still trust its coverage. Jordan-Hare will have some real juice too, with belief injected into Auburn's season. However, LSU's down-to-down edge should create separation over 60 minutes. TOP PICK LSU vs Auburn Over/Under pick: Under 51.5 The Under is my top pick in this matchup and I'd play it to 49.5. Brown is producing 0.41 EPA per rush, fourth among qualified runners, and a heavy quarterback-run plan is the best way to keep the game close . That also bleeds clock. LSU's defense has held opponents to 4.35 yards per play and a 39.2% success rate, while Auburn's unit ranks 31st in adjusted EPA allowed and gives up 5.15 yards per snap . LSU's offense is good, but its opponent-adjusted efficiency ranks 25th rather than among the elite. Also, I still have not seen enough from Sam Leavitt to trust him to make game-defining plays. I don't think his head coach has either. LSU can control field position and reach the low 30s. Auburn landing in the teens leaves enough room for Under 51.5. LSU vs Auburn combo The prevailing theme throughout is LSU's defense. It controls the game, wins the game for the Tigers, and keeps it low-scoring throughout. That holds true early on, which is why I added the first-quarter Under to this combo beyond the previously mentioned two plays. I don't expect either team to come out guns blazing through the air due to decision-making concerns tied to the quarterback. That's particularly true early in the game when the emphasis on either to score quickly is minimal. That should keep the clock running most of the first quarter and start off this heavily correlated combo out strong. Can the Auburn Tigers pull off another upset in Year 1 under coach Alex Golesh? Auburn pulled off the biggest upset of the college football season by defeating No. 1 Georgia this past Saturday in Athens. Now, it turns its attention to the LSU Tigers as a team with confidence that has proven it can beat anyone. Auburn enters this game as the underdog. Correspondingly, the ESPN matchup predictor gives Auburn a 28.8% chance to win. Auburn will need to play the type of game it did against Georgia. It will need to control the line of scrimmage and consistently run the football. Auburn outgained Georgia 192-113 on the ground. The LSU Tigers are No. 1 in the conference in run defense, allowing just 88.1 yards per game on the ground. However, the Bulldogs are No. 2 in that category, and Auburn had success with Byrum Brown and the running backs. The turnover battle will be key once again. Auburn forced three turnovers against Georgia and did not commit any. Going into that game, interceptions had been an issue for Brown with seven on the season. Auburn will be facing a quarterback in Sam Leavitt who has thrown eight interceptions this season. The Auburn defense will need to create opportunities for the offense to gain an upset victory. A big advantage for Auburn is it is at home. Both of LSU's losses were away from Baton Rouge: at Ole Miss and at Kentucky. The crowd at Jordan-Hare should be electric on Saturday after Week 7's upset win at Georgia. LSU is coming off a dominant 31-0 shutout victory over Mississippi State, bouncing back in impressive fashion after a disappointing overtime loss to Kentucky. Quarterback Sam Leavitt delivered one of his best performances of the season, completing 31 of 38 passes for 289 yards and four touchdowns and no interceptions. The Tigers' defense was equally impressive, keeping the Bulldogs off the scoreboard and securing LSU's first shutout against an SEC opponent since 2007. Meanwhile, Auburn enters this matchup with plenty of momentum after pulling off a stunning 27-24 upset over No. 1 Georgia on the road. The victory gave Auburn a major confidence boost heading into another SEC showdown. For LSU, the focus now shifts to Jordan-Hare Stadium, where the Tigers will look to build on Saturday's dominant win in a challenging road environment. LSU has yet to win away from Death Valley this season, making Saturday's matchup another important test for Lane Kiffin and the team. With the SEC race heating up, the Tigers will need another complete performance to secure their first road victory of the season. What the LSU coach thinks Can LSU football QB Sam Leavitt keep a clean sheet? When junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has avoided turnovers, LSU has easily won this season. Last time out against Mississippi State, Leavitt took care of the football and worked efficiently and smart. It paid off with a 31-0 victory. Auburn has been opportunistic this season when teams have turned the ball over. Georgia fumbled late in the game last weekend, allowing Auburn to go down and kick a game-winning field goal as time expired to pull off the upset in Athens. Kiffin said earlier this week that he and his staff will highlight the importance of ball security. "As you breakdown your losses and close losses, they're usually not as much about how many plays they make," Kiffin said. "It's more the mistakes you make, and the penalties, more false starts and more turnovers than when you play at home." LSU football offensive staff familiar with Auburn QB Byrum Brown When LSU offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. was South Florida's offensive coordinator under then-head coach Jeff Scott, he helped open up the recruiting process to bring Brown to the Bulls . So Weiss is familiar with Brown's game as LSU gears up for this matchup. "Really hard player to tackle, similar to playing (South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers) that way. They're different styles, but they're really strong through a lot of arm tackles," Kiffin said of Brown. "He seems really smart by the way that he plays." Brown played for Auburn head coach Alex Golesh at South Florida before following him to The Plains out of the transfer portal. LSU offense should get plenty of opportunities It's hard to score if the offense doesn't have the ball or the ability to extend drives with it. Through six games, Auburn ranks 133rd in college football in time of possession. At 26:54, Auburn is dead-last in the SEC in time of possession. But the situation is not quite like that with Ole Miss , which is second-to-last in the league in time of possession because it operates and scores quickly. Auburn scores just 26.8 points per game, which comes in 13th out of 16 teams in the SEC. While Auburn does convert third downs 46% of the time, its offense only converts touchdowns in the red zone at a 65% clip. Defenses have racked up 23 sacks against Auburn and have caused 15 Auburn turnovers to this point. All of that adds up to LSU's offense likely winning the time of possession battle. The onus, then, will be on LSU to cap drives with points. Lane Kiffin vs first-year head coaches this season It's a small sample size, but Kiffin has not found success against teams with first-year head coaches this season. It also happens that the two matchups with coaches in their first year at their programs were LSU's two road games so far this season. Still, LSU lost both of those road games at Ole Miss against Pete Golding and at Kentucky against Will Stein. That same trend is presenting itself Kiffin again, this time it's Golesh at Auburn. Golesh was the coach at South Florida from 2023 to 2025 before taking the Auburn job over the offseason. While at USF, Golesh hosted Saban and Alabama in 2023 and pushed the Crimson Tide to the brink before falling 17-3. So, this game likely won't be easy for LSU. Kiffin will look to buck the trend against Golesh at Auburn this weekend. LSU football vs Auburn prediction If you are a believer in trap games or letdown spots, LSU's road game at Auburn is a hard game to handicap. One could argue this is a trap game for LSU — also factor that this game kicks of at 11 a.m. — while Auburn comes into the showdown off the program's biggest win in some time, knocking off No. 1 Georgia on the road. Only thing that feels certain about this game is that Jordan-Hare will be rocking and odd things take place in that building. Look for an ugly, sloppy, sleepy game. LSU squeaks one out in the end. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brooks Crew Thu, October 22, 2026 at 9:04 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Auburn Tigers are red-hot after their stunning win against No. 1 Georgia last week, but they will not have any time to rest on their laurels, as up next for Alex Golesh's squad is a big-time matchup with LSU, and early predictions are not in the Tigers' favor. As it stands, the Tigers are a seven-point underdog to their rival Tigers, though CBS Sports' Austin Nivison believes the Tigers will lose by at least 10 points . Here's why. "What Auburn did last week will be commendable -- and fans will remember it forever -- but it was also extremely improbable," he wrote. "Georgia out-gained Auburn by 74 yards, and the Tigers barely pulled out a win despite a plus-3 turnover margin. LSU's defense is athletic enough to contain Brown, and the offense is capable of putting up big numbers. It's possible the crowd and Auburn defense give Sam Leavitt trouble, but LSU is capable of winning this game by double digits." In fact, every CBS analyst polled about the game took Lane Kiffin's squad to win straight-up, but a few, like Chip Patterson and David Cobb, predicted the Tigers to at least cover the spread. It's certainly a difficult matchup for the Tigers, who could be experiencing what Kiffin called 'relief syndrome' after their win against Georgia. There is a path to the Tigers winning this game, though, and it seems to run through Byrum Brown. "If Auburn is going to put its best foot forward this weekend -- and for the rest of the season -- Brown will have to use his legs to create offense," Nivison continued. "That worked last week in Athens... The catch is that Brown will be exposed to more hits, which increases his risk for injury. Because of that, if Auburn can get its traditional run game rolling, that takes some of the workload off Brown's legs." Brown seemed to have been contained a bit in earlier games, as his number was called for design plays quite rarely, but against the Dawgs, Auburn offensive coordinator Joel Gordon leaned on Brown's legs to get the Tigers' offense moving. It worked to great effect last week, but LSU will now be even more prepared for Brown's dual-threat nature, which adds a layer of complexity to the Tigers' playcalling this week. The Tigers, coming off a marquee win, are looking to continue their momentum, and having home-field advantage should play a big part in their matchup with Kiffin's Tigers. However, LSU has answers for most of Auburn's offensive production, so the Tigers will likely need to get creative if they want to emerge from the Tiger Bowl with a win. away.headline: Early SEC availability report for Auburn's SEC game vs. LSU revealed
away.blurb: The initial SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report is out for this week's matchup between the Auburn Tigers and the No. 17 LSU Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium, and Auburn will enter the game with a relatively clean bill of health. Offensive lineman Tai Buster and tight end Hunter Herring remain "out" for Auburn, which has been the case since SEC play began in Week 3. However, one addition has been made. Defensive lineman Saint Farrior is listed as "questionable" for Saturday's game against LSU, meaning it is uncertain as of Wednesday whether he will be available to play. LSU will be without linebacker Will Weeks, safety Dashawn Speans, wide receiver Phillip Wright, and linebacker Charles Ross on Saturday, while defensive tackle Richard Anderson is listed as "doubtful." Wright is the most notable name on the report with three catches for 70 yards and a touchdown in LSU's season-opening win at Clemson. He has not played since Week 2 against Louisiana Tech. Linebacker Whit Weeks will miss his fourth straight game after he suffered a leg fracture in LSU's win over Texas A&M last month. Despite several players being out, LSU got good news Wednesday as wide receiver Jackson Harris, tight end Trey'Dez Green, and defensive end Princewill Umanmielen were left off the initial availability report and are expected to play this Saturday at Auburn. Harris leads LSU wide receivers with 456 yards and five touchdowns, and Green has 222 receiving yards and a touchdown this season. Umanmielen, who followed head coach Lane Kiffin from Ole Miss, leads the team in sacks with eight and is fourth in tackles with 27. Farrior played three snaps in Auburn's win over Georgia last week and has played in just four games this season for 17 total snaps. According to the SEC's website, "SEC school personnel must submit availability reports three days before each football game, with daily updates leading to a final report 90 minutes prior to game time." Inaccurate reports could result in fines between $25,000 and $100,000. Auburn will face LSU on Saturday at 11 a.m. CT. Taylor Jones is the lead writer for Auburn Wire, part of the USA TODAY Network. Pete Fiutak Fri, October 23, 2026 at 6:10 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads All of a sudden, South Carolina has become the proverbial Team You Don't Want To Face. It was only one game a few weeks ago in horrendous conditions, but the Gamecocks' 38-19 win over Florida showed one thing more than anything else – they're still trying. This was supposed to be a big bounceback season for South Carolina, but it lost three straight SEC games, including an overtime home game to Kentucky, and that was it. No SEC title, no CFP appearance. It was all over, and it wasn't even the second week of October. This is a good Gamecock team in the fun make-lemonade-out-of-the-season position of getting to screw everyone else up. Tennessee has to keep its focus and show that it's worthy of being in the mix for all the things South Carolina was supposed to be fighting for right now. It beat Alabama, it took out Auburn by ten, and it probably should've beaten Texas. Now it has to sidestep the landmine. Tennessee vs South Carolina: Quick Hits The Vols get a week off before hosting Kentucky, and then they're off to Texas A&M. South Carolina goes to Oklahoma next week before hosting Texas A&M. The two haven't played since Tennessee won 41-20 in 2023. The Vols are 4-1 in the last five meetings. The Tennessee running game was okay in the win over Alabama, and George MacIntyre kept his cool, throwing for close to 200 yards. But the offense turned it over twice and was hardly smooth. The Volunteer defense held Bama to 201 yards of total offense and forced four takeaways because of the ten tackles for loss and five sacks that dominated the game. Tennessee is No. 1 in the nation in sacks, and it's about to force the Gamecocks into a whole slew of mistakes. Why South Carolina Will Win How did South Carolina blow out Florida? LaNorris Sellers showed the upside to be a dangerous NFL quarterback. The offense didn't turn the ball over, and the defense pitched a gem, especially against the run. Tennessee has a good offense, but it's the defense that delivers the mail. South Carolina can't get frustrated. It needs to keep the mistakes to a bare minimum and be okay with living to fight another day. Tennessee vs South Carolina Prediction, Betting Lines It is possible to run on the Tennessee defense. It'll get its sacks and plays behind the line, but Auburn was able to run well against the Vols. It lost because it turned the ball over three times. Arch Manning was actually okay against the Vols, but the two Texas turnovers and 11 penalties made it way too close. The weather had a lot to do with the three Florida turnovers against South Carolina. It's going to be 72 and sunny on Saturday in Columbia. picks.headline: ‘Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Tennessee vs South Carolina matchup
picks.blurb: ‘Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama' – ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Tennessee vs South Carolina matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Randy Sartin-Imagn Images Zach Ragan Tue, October 20, 2026 at 4:52 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Tennessee Volunteers will travel to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against the South Carolina Gamecocks. Tennessee is facing one of its scariest tests of the season this weekend. After dominating Alabama last weekend in Knoxville, the Vols are set to head to Columbia this weekend for a matchup against South Carolina. It's a classic trap game for Tennessee in a stadium that's been a house of horrors for the program over the last two decades (the Vols are just 2-6 in Columbia since 2008, and one of those wins came in 2020 when fan attendance was limited due to Covid). South Carolina is coming off a bye week after a big road win against Florida earlier this month. ESPN's Greg McElroy picks winner of Tennessee vs South Carolina ESPN's Greg McElroy, who called the Vols' win over Alabama last weekend, thinks Tennessee will falter in Columbia on Saturday. McElroy has South Carolina beating Tennessee 27-24. "Can South Carolina stop the run that keeps Tennessee on schedule?" said McElroy. "Tennessee has 46 runs of 10 or more yards. That's top nine in the country, and Josh Heupel's teams are 71-9 when they run for 150 yards or more. Look, South Carolina is pretty stingy on those runs. So this is strength against strength, and the pick kind of tilts on whether Tennessee's quarterback can hold up his end of the bargain. "I'm going to take South Carolina to win this game 27-24. I think they're going to win on the ground. They're also coming off a bye. Tennessee just went to war last week against Alabama. They looked amazing doing it, but we've seen teams elevate and then come back to earth the following week, and I think that could happen for Tennessee right here. Because (Matt) Fuller and (LaNorris) Sellers are going to get yards when that first defender misses. Tennessee's linebackers cannot afford to miss in this game. So that (Fuller and Sellers) will keep the Gamecocks out of third and long — which is where Tennessee's sacks live. It shrinks those pass rushing opportunities that are Tennessee's very best weapon." "Tennessee's defense is amazing," added McElroy. "They're sixth in points per drive. They're gonna make this thing super tight. But I just lean towards the Gamecocks in this game and the potential flat spot for the Volunteers — even though they bring the better defense into the matchup. The Gamecocks bring a run game and receivers that can win one-on-one. So we will take the Gamecocks." Vols fans won't love that pick, but it's hard to blame McElroy, who has been pretty accurate with his predictions this season, based on Tennessee's past history in Columbia. Tennessee and South Carolina will kick off at 3:30 PM ET on Saturday. The game will air on ESPN. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. picks.headline: Tennessee-South Carolina predictions: Why are Gamecocks favored over Vols?
picks.blurb: Tennessee is coming off a massive win over Alabama . So naturally, South Carolina is favored over the Volunteers in Saturday's matchup in Columbia. The Gamecocks had a week to relish in their impressive road upset of Florida and rest up during their bye, while many are expecting a Vols letdown after such an emotional high and a field-storming last week. SEC letdowns have been popular this season: Ole Miss lost to Florida after beating LSU. Florida lost to Missouri after beating Ole Miss. Georgia lost to Auburn after beating Alabama . And there's a reason Tennessee fans are more worried than you think fans of the 11th-ranked team playing a 3-3 team should be. The Vols' last trip to Columbia in 2022 ended with a blowout loss that knocked them out of College Football Playoff contention. Tennessee vs South Carolina predictions, expert picks USA TODAY Sports staff picks : John Brice: Tennessee Matt Hayes: South Carolina Jordan Mendoza: South Carolina Paul Myerberg: Tennessee Erick Smith: South Carolina Eddie Timanus: South Carolina Blake Toppmeyer: Tennessee Austin Curtright: South Carolina 31, Tennessee 27 John Leuzzi: South Carolina 24, Tennessee 21 Jordan Mendoza: South Carolina 26, Tennessee 23 LaNorris Sellers was awesome in leading the Gamecocks to an upset of Florida two weeks ago. He threw four touchdown passes and averaged eight yards per attempt. George MacIntyre was … fine as the Volunteers took down Alabama, primarily with a dominant defensive effort. It’s hard not to lean toward Sellers, as it looks like he might be getting hot. South Carolina 27, Tennessee 17 — Adam Bittner, USA TODAY Sports This is a major trap game for Tennessee on the road after an emotional win, but its defense should travel just fine. The matchup may be decided by who's better between Vols running back DeSean Bishop and the Gamecocks' run defense that ranks third in the SEC. Oddsmakers slightly favor South Carolina in a spot that feels ripe for an unranked-over-ranked result. Still, picking against Tennessee's defense has been a fool's errand. Tennessee 24, South Carolina 21 . — Emmett Siegal, Knoxville News Sentinel Tennessee's win over Alabama is nothing to ignore but South Carolina also had a statement win right before an extra week to get healthy with the open date. The Vols keep it close but the home crowd and older quarterback prevail. South Carolina 24, Tennessee 17 . — Lulu Kesin, Greenville News Tennessee-South Carolina injury report After South Carolina was missing starting defensive back Quay'sheed Scott, defensive lineman Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy, edge rusher Julian Walker and starting center Carter Miller against Florida on Oct. 10, only Miller and Scott of the four are on the report this week. Scott is doubtful and Miller is listed as questionable. There were no new injured Tennessee players listed on the initial SEC student-athlete availability report for the game against South Carolina. However, seven Tennessee players have already suffered season-ending injuries: starting left guard Wendell Moe ; starting safety Edrees Farooq (knee); starting tight end Ethan Davis (knee); safety Dylan Lewis (foot); wide receiver/kick returner Joakim Dodson (leg); linebacker Jaedon Harmon (knee); and cornerback Jadais Richard (upper-body). Is South Carolina favored vs Tennessee? Betting odds, spread (via BetMGM ) Favorite : South Carolina by 2 points Over/under : 50.5 total points Moneyline : South Carolina -130, Tennessee +110 Who will start at QB for Tennessee: George MacIntyre or Faizon Brandon? Josh Heupel refused to name a starter for Saturday's game, but the Vols will likely stick with George MacIntyre under center for a third straight game. MacIntyre is 2-0 as a starter and completed 21-of-31 passes for 197 yards and an interception in Tennessee's 26-10 win over Alabama last week. Faizon Brandon, who won the starting QB job out of camp, dressed but did not play vs. the Crimson Tide. "MacIntyre … you see him continuing to get better each and every week," Shane Beamer said . "With his ability to run the offense, get rid of the ball when it's not there in the passing game, sit in the pocket, throw the ball downfield, but make good decisions and continue to play winning football. And that's what I think both those guys are doing a great job of is playing winning football.” Is Dylan Stewart playing vs Tennessee? Is South Carolina star pass rusher back from suspension? Yes The Gamecocks edge rusher returned for the Florida game after serving a one-game suspension for multiple incidents in South Carolina's Sept. 26 loss to Alabama, which included punching a Crimson Tide player. Against Florida, Stewart had his best performance of the season, with five tackles (four solo), two forced fumbles, one sack and one tackle for loss. Pro Football Focus gave him a career-best 95.8 grade for his defense and a 92.7 pressure grade, the second-highest in his three seasons. "He was awesome throughout the game, his impact on the field is evident," Shane Beamer said. "He's a special talent in the way that he's able to affect other teams' offenses . . . I thought he did a great job, not just against the pass, but I really think thought he played the run well, just fitting gaps and being where he was supposed to be. "... "This will be a huge couple weeks for him and should see an even better version of him against Tennessee." What channel is Tennessee-South Carolina game on? away.blurb: MANHATTAN — Kansas State quarterback Avery Johnson returned to the game after missing one play that resulted in a touchdown. The quarterback was slow to get up after a 59-yard run that set up a four-yard rushing touchdown by Rodney Fields. Backup Jacob Knuth entered the game to hand the ball off to Fields with 13:46 left in the first quarter. Johnson lay on the turf for several minutes before being pulled up by the trainers. He smiled as he got up and had no noticeable limp . At the end of the 59-yard run, he stumbled before falling to the turf. Kansas ' Bryson Hayes returned the ensuing kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown to tie the game at seven with 13:04 left in the opening quarter. On Johnson's first play back, he completed a 45-yard pass to a wide-open Derrick Salley downfield. The Wildcats ran a designed run for Johnson two plays later. Wyatt D. away.blurb: The Wildcats are in desperate need of someone to step in for Oakley. He was the leading receiver at the position for K-State a year ago. This season, he is among the top players on the roster with NFL interest. During training camp, Klein said he hosted several NFL scouts who were on campus to check out Oakley. Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAB F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on Here's Latest Injury Update On Kansas State Wildcats TE Garrett Oakley (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) Shandel Richardson Tue, October 20, 2026 at 3:50 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas State Wildcats are expected to once again be without one of their key offensive players this weekend on the road against the Arizona State Sun Devils. K-State coach Collin Klein hinted that tight end Garrett Oakley could miss the third game of the Big 12 conference schedule. Oakley did not play in last week's game against the Kansas Jayhawks in the Sunflower Showdown at Bill Snyder Family Stadium. Here's what Klein had to say during his weekly press conference about the Oakley situation. "Probably unlikely, but we'll see," Klein said. "Day to day." Oakley missed the game because of an undisclosed illness. It gave more opportunities to sophomore Linkon Cure, who is among the most hyped players in program history. He is the first five-star recruit to ever play at Kansas State. While he has gotten off to a slow start, the Wildcats are hoping he can live up to the huge expectations. He has seven catches for 66 yards this season. Last week he caught two passes for 16 yards. The Wildcats need production from Cure because Oakley isn't the only tight end missing. Two weeks ago, it was announced that backup Will Anciaux would miss the season after sustaining a lower leg injury. Klein is also experimenting with moving left tackle Oliver Miller to tight end. That's where he played last week in the win against the Jayhawks. It is unknown if the move is permanent but that's where Miller will play this week. This was a move that was in the works because the Wildcats coaching staff was using him at tight end the past few weeks. A 6-foot-6 freshman, Miller has embraced the opportunity. He was a standout at Cherry Creek (Colo.) High School, where he was rated the No. 41 tackle in the country. Perhaps this could be a better calling for him because of his athleticism. The hope is Oakley is back in uniform sooner than later. He is a big component of the offense and is needed if the Wildcats are going to remain in the hunt for the Big 12 conference championship and College Football Playoff.

picks.headline: What an Advanced Model Predicts in Clemson's ACC Matchup with Virginia Tech
picks.blurb: What an Advanced Model Predicts in Clemson's ACC Matchup with Virginia Tech Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM TIGERS FB SI.COM TIGERS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET BASKETBALL NEWS Saturday night marks a crossroads for the Clemson Tigers and head coach Dabo Swinney, who welcome in the Virginia Tech Hokies in a highly-anticpated matchup. Memorial Stadium should be sold out this weekend, and Swinney will look to continue the strong stretch coming out of the open date. However, when looking at the advanced analytics, it could mean that Clemson has to survive a strong test from the Hokies to pick up its third ACC win of the season. Fortunately for fans, there tends to be a lean towards the Tigers in that department, according to Versus Sports Simulator . It gives Clemson a 64% chance to win on Saturday, with an average score being around 29-23. This contest has been one that has constantly switched in the projections, due to the losses that both teams have had since the month of October began. Virginia Tech had a two-game skid against Pitt and Cal, losing by a score in both games, to be forced to win out for the remainder of the season. However, when the month began, the Tigers only had a 53% chance to win. The model gives Swinney’s group a defense with a B+ grade, while the offense is generously given a B- grade. That’s how Clemson has won games over the course of this season, with the defense leaving enough points on the board for the Tigers to score on sporadic occasions. On the flip side, Virginia Tech is given a C+ overall ranking by Versus, with its best quality being a B- offense. However, it’s important to note that the Hokies’ defense, although graded a C+, leads the country in tackles for loss and is also first in the ACC in sacks and forced fumbles. Regardless, Clemson is expected to hit the ground running, with this amount being the most it has scored against a Power Four opponent at all this season. The home-field advantage plays a small factor in the Tigers' favor, with betting markets having them favored by about a field goal. Even with the game being at Memorial Stadium, Versus has Clemson as the favorite regardless of where the game is. If the game were at Lane Stadium, Swinney’s group would have a 52% chance to win the game on Saturday. However, there’s much more to a game than the model itself, but the advanced analytics show advantages on Clemson’s end that perhaps others aren’t thinking about. Swinney will look to reinforce that at home on Saturday, playing a team that will be playing with hopes to remain in the ACC Championship contention pool. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. and the game will be broadcast on ESPN. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images C_Craft Fri, October 23, 2026 at 1:41 PM UTC · 11 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Nitty Gritty Time Has Arrived for 2026 Greetings once again STS readers! Dabo Swinney always says each week is the "biggest game of the year" but even he has conceded that some games have more juice than others. This would have to be considered one of those games. While it isn't on the scale of a top-ten matchup, or even what it might have been back in 2011 when Clemson traveled to face VT or when they saw the Hokies again in the ACC title game, it is a vital tipping point for both teams looking to regain relevance. The winner of this game stays firmly in the hunt for a chance to go to Charlotte. Reaching 10 wins would be a huge accomplishment for this year's Tigers, and despite the two lopsided losses, it would be a step back up after 2025's major letdown. Before we get to the matchup, here is my good, bad, and ugly from last week's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern. The Good: Clemson's defense was lights out beyond a few moments during CSU's first drive when their scripted plays found some success ahead of a missed FG attempt. I was most encouraged by how well the depth performed, particularly in the secondary, as they got subbed more and more into the game. The upgrade in secondary execution across the board cannot be understated after last year's debacles. Clemson's special teams continues to shine week in and week out. I said Chris Johnson, Jr. was on the verge of scoring a kickoff return and nearly did it on his one opportunity. Nolan Hauser continues to look like an NFL starter and the coverage team produced a turnover for a touchdown for loyal Tiger Kylon Griffin. The Bad: Red zone offense wasn't ugly because the Tigers did punch in touchdown runs from CJJ and Gideon Davidson, but obviously there were more missed chances and bad penalties that continue to haunt this year's offense inside the 20 yard line. 37 points easily could have been 57 points or more considering the defensive and special teams dominance. The Ugly: Clemson's downfield passing attack gets the nod for the ugly. Especially when Tait Reynolds delivered plenty of throws that were there for big-money WRs TJ Moore and Bryant Wesco. Reynolds also apparently missed Moore running wide open on a post at least once, but lack of WR production and TDs were not on Chad Morris's play calls. He's getting 1 on 1 scenarios for the outside guys and they need to pay those off the way they are being paid to do. Clemson can't afford to miss those in these next stretch of games. Now that we are done with that, on to the 5-2 Hokies. Clemson Offense vs. VT Defense: There are several reasons to have some apprehension as a Clemson fan looking at this game. Clemson's running attack has proven to be much further along than the downfield passing game. It isn't a coincidence that Clemson has run the ball effectively in the 4 wins and failed miserably to do so in the 2 losses. Clemson's passing attack has yet to prove it can go win if it has to and VT's defense has been good against the run so far this season. They have given up a lot of passing yards, however, but can Reynolds and the offense deliver enough to exploit that apparent weakness? Any DC with a functional brain is going to try to force Reynolds to throw to win, which will mean loading up on the run and sending pressures regularly. Clemson fans are going to get another real sign if the OL has gotten its act together more with the new (and reportedly best) group of five guys out there together. VT is a pressure defense and looks to force the issue which has helped them rack up good sack and TFL numbers as well as effective run defense, but likewise has opened them up to getting burned on explosives (especially in the passing game). Clemson desperately needs to hit on the explosive play chances that are going to be there and, of course, limit VT's ability to get them behind the chains. Dabo has harped on the team not winning the turnover margin in games this season. Clemson is certainly due to do that, but it starts with the offense not turning it over. Clemson ended up throwing the ball 44 times in the Miami game, and that number needs to be between 25-30 this week I think if Clemson is going to win. This team is not equipped to play shootout football right now, and VT is much more capable of that and has had those types of games already. Reynolds has cut down on putting the ball in jeopardy, and a big part of that is having better pass protection to begin with, but he's been a little loose with the ball as a runner. Reynolds managed to avoid a bad turnover last week when he pounced on his own fumble, but the margin of error is not big in any of these remaining games to overcome putting the ball on the ground. I discussed the Moore/Wesco duo earlier, but it is imperative one or both deliver and win their matchups that VT is going to present them with in order to try to force Clemson away from the running game. I liked a lot of the concepts Morris showed to get the ball to the outside guys in various ways, including using bootlegs with Wesco coming across where you traditionally use a tight end. TJ Moore has been best on the slant in the RPO game, but he needs to win more of the outside fade situations that he has not been nearly as good with this season. Gordon Sellars is out with a concussion, and that eliminates at least one of the plan B options that Chad Morris very thinly veiled that he desired to have to push Moore when he has his press conference on Wednesday. Clemson needs the 2024 Texas game or 2025 SMU game version of TJ Moore on Saturday night. VT is similar in some ways to Miami defensively in that their front is stronger than their secondary. Clemson was unable to exploit Miami enough outside to offset being beaten at the point of attack that night. Clemson still needs to get at least 100 net yards rushing to keep that part of the offense relevant. The running back room is plenty good enough to deliver with Jay Haynes now back with Davidson and Johnson. They need to be given ample chances to deliver in this game. Clemson Defense vs. VT Offense : Clemson's defense is certainly ahead of the offense in the growth department. Part of this is because the big money guys on this side of the ball are playing like they are big money guys more consistently. This will be a real test considering VT has at least one playmaker at WR, RB, and TE to go with an NFL prospect at QB. Clemson has to make sure that VT can't get its running game going with Jeffrey Overton because he can hurt you badly if you let him get loose. BC found this out in nasty weather when Overton cooked them for 209 yards. Pittsburgh escaped with a win over the Hokies despite giving up nearly 500 yards of offense and 33 points, but one big reason was VT couldn't run the ball and passing more led to more turnovers. Ethan Grunkemeyer is a good player as Clemson fans saw last year when he handled the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl, but you still want him having to attack the strength of Clemson's back end versus having the balance of the running game to set things up and protect him. I worry the most about VT using Overton in the screen game and their dynamic tight end Luke Reynolds because those guys will match up with Clemson's nickel, safeties, or linebackers and not Ashton Hampton or Elliot Washington. It will be vital to make Grunkemeyer hold the ball so the rush can get there and get hands in the passing lanes on VT's RPO game. VT can be turned over, but that depends a lot on getting them into more obvious passing scenarios and heating Grunkemeyer up. Penn State was able to manage enough of a run game and largely keep Clemson's depleted defensive front from bothering him last year in the bowl game. He can really hurt you if you let him stand there and get through his reads. Clemson isn't going to keep VT under 100 yards and shut them out like they did CSU unless they deliver in some crazy way that far surpasses expectations. VT has too much talent to not have some success, but Clemson's ability to turn them over and force field goal attempts will be massive. Clemson can win a game in the 20s, but allowing VT to get to 30 or more probably means a big fat L for the Tigers on Saturday night. Getting VT at home helps for sure because they have been way better in Lane Stadium than on the road, such as when they allowed a depleted California squad to take them down. VT has been a fast-starting team, which usually means they are good at their opening 12-15 play script, so Clemson needs to be locked in right away on defense. Special Teams: Most fans who have been around since the 2000s know how much special teams helped Frank Beamer elevate VT to a top 20 program. It certainly was a major factor when Clemson lost a critical game with the Hokies back in 2007. Ironically, now the Tigers have the differential special teams play heading into this matchup thanks to outstanding work across the board under Rich Bisaccia. Returns look dangerous, coverage has been largely terrific, and Nolan Hauser has to be among the frontrunners for the Lou Groza Award. This game is pretty close on paper for sure, so this phase could be the difference. None of Clemson's games has featured a special teams fake this season, so Clemson has to be alert. Fortunately there hasn't really been any reason for Clemson to try to get fancy on returns or on kicks. The closest thing was Nolan Hauser's pooch punt at California that paid off with a roughing penalty, but that is exactly why you run something like that on a defense that isn't prepped to defend a punt. Overall: There is a lot about this 2026 team that reminds me of the 2021 team. I ended up really liking that 21 team mainly because they showed real toughness to overcome the obvious warts and squeezed 10 wins out of a team that easily could have only won 7. That isn't what you want year in and year out as a fan, especially when "Best is the Standard" is written in your facility, but this team has always been more about getting back to being tough. The VTScoop staff make their score predictions for Virginia Tech's game against Clemson (Photo: Haden Tolbert, 247Sports) One of the most anticipated games of Virginia Tech's 2026 schedule has arrived. The Virginia Tech Hokies (5-2, 2-2 ACC) travel to face off against the Clemson Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) in pivotal mid-season matchup with plenty of short and long term implications. Virginia Tech is coming off a homecoming victory, winning 34-24, against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets to stop a two game skid. Meanwhile, Clemson took care of FCS opponent Charleston Southern 37-0 after enjoying an early Open Week the weekend prior. The two teams have met 37 times in both programs histories with Clemson holding the 24-12-1 edge. The Tigers enter the matchup with a 7-win streak in the series dating back to 2011. The two teams will face off for their fourth time in the last decade on Saturday. Saturday will mark the first meeting between James Franklin and Dabo Swinney as opposing head coaches. However, there is plenty of familiarity between the two programs. Penn State defeated Clemson, 22-10, in the 2025 Pinstripe Bowl, and several players from that matchup will take the field again on Saturday. Clemson defensive coordinator Tom Allen also spent the 2024 season as Franklin's defensive coordinator at Penn State. This matchup has been circled on Virginia Tech's schedule since it was first announced, and now the Hokies have an opportunity to deliver a statement on one of the ACC's biggest stages. With both programs looking to establish themselves in the conference hierarchy, Saturday's showdown carries implications that extend beyond this season. Can Virginia Tech capitalize on the opportunity and make a statement about the direction of Franklin's program, or will Clemson defend its home turf and reaffirm its place among the ACC's best? Related : 2026 VTScoop Virginia Tech Hokies Midseason Predictions The game will be held inside Memorial Stadium in Clemson, South Carolina with kickoff set for 7:00 PM EST. The game will be broadcast on ESPN and streamed on fuboTV . Ahead of the game, VTSCOOP's Evan G. Watkins, Doug Bowman, Amber Marie, Andrew Alix, Jacob Maggard, Haden Tolbert and Matej Sis put together their predictions for the game. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Evan G. Watkins Last week I predicted Virginia Tech would win this weekend, which was a deviation from my summer predictions. I haven't seen enough consistency from Clemson for me to confidently predict them to win, and with it basically becoming a pick 'em in Vegas (Clemson -2.5 at the time of writing this), I'm rolling with the Hokies. Extra juice for my prediction - John Love walks it off. Prediction: Virginia Tech 27 , Clemson 24 Admittedly, the more I look at this matchup on paper, the more I like the Hokies. This is arguably the closest these two programs have been in terms of quality in quite some time. If there was ever a statement game for Virginia Tech to change the hierarchy of the ACC and announce itself as a legitimate contender, this is it. Clemson has been tough to watch offensively and hasn't shown the consistency or explosiveness needed to expose Virginia Tech's bend-but-don't-break defense. On the other side of the ball, Ethan Grunkemeyer has both familiarity and success against Tom Allen's defense, which should only help as he continues his scorching-hot start. That said, the game is not played on paper. This will be a difficult environment against an extremely talented team. Despite liking several of the matchups, it only takes a few defensive breakdowns — something we've seen far too often from Virginia Tech — for Clemson to take control. I also believe this is easily the best defense the Hokies have faced to date, and the combination of offensive line concerns and an inconsistent running game gives me pause. This feels like a game that will come down to the wire. If Virginia Tech plays its most complete game of the season, I believe it has the potential to leave Clemson with a convincing win. But until the Hokies prove they can beat a quality opponent on the road, especially in an environment like Death Valley, I'm not quite ready to make that leap. Prediction: Virginia Tech 23, Clemson 26 Clemson isn't anywhere close to as good as they once were. But I'm still not completely sold on this Virginia Tech team traveling to a tough environment and getting the victory. With the struggles on the offensive line and in the secondary, I just can't pick them to win a game like this until they prove it. It'll be close, but I think Tech's weaknesses prove to be just enough of a difference on the road. Prediction: Virginia Tech 23, Clemson 24 I'll be honest - I'm struggling with this one. It's truly a toss up. Clemson's passing struggles open the door for the Hokies' stout run defense to shut their offense down. However, recent VT offensive line injuries leave pass protection vulnerable and the run game has been inconsistent at best. So how do we have any idea what's going to happen? Again with the honesty: I don't. In true toss ups, I tend to favor the home team, so that's what I'm going with. Could Virginia Tech pull off an upset on the road? Absolutely. But I need to see the Hokies come out on top in these situations before I believe it. Prediction: Virginia Tech 20, Clemson 27 This game is a tough one for me to grapple with. It's easy to ride the highs of the win against Georgia Tech, but even that victory exposed some of our defensive issues. Before the season, I would have chalked this up as a highly probable loss, but I'm not necessarily there anymore, given Clemson's struggles in the passing game. I mean, two touchdown passes all year? What a waste of talent on the outside. With that being said, we've seen Virginia Tech face backup quarterbacks against Pitt and Cal and somehow make guys who played incompetently against other competition suddenly look like All-Americans. To me, the biggest tests are Virginia Tech's secondary, its pass rush, and how Ethan Grunkemeyer and company fare against the most talented defense they've faced all season. I want to be optimistic, and a Virginia Tech win wouldn't surprise me. But in a matchup between two talented, multifaceted, and ultimately flawed teams, I'll give the edge to Clemson and that Saturday night Death Valley environment. To be the man, you've got to beat the man. And until Virginia Tech proves it can win a game like this, I'll believe it when I see it. Hopefully, that's Saturday night. Prediction: Virginia Tech 21, Clemson 24 Jacob Maggard Virginia Tech got back on schedule with a victory over the Yellow Jackets. James Franklin has put an emphasis on fixing the mistakes and the Hokies did that with only four penalties for 40 yards. The Hokies will have to continue limiting the mistakes against the best defense they've faced this year. Clemson has struggled to pass the ball no matter who's in at quarterback. Tait Reynolds is a true freshman and he simply looks like he's not ready to start games for the Clemson Tigers. He has one passing touchdown on the season with three interceptions and is averaging less than seven yards per pass attempt. The struggles are not all on him. The offensive line has struggled protecting Reynolds and they've held back Gideon Davidson as well. Davidson has proven his ability to make big plays like the 75-yard rushing touchdown he had against Cal. The Hokies have one of the best defensive lines in the country and I believe they're the key to this game. Pressure Reynolds and do not allow him to be comfortable in the pocket. They have to rack up the TFLs as well and limit Davidson's big play ability. The Hokies offense will be challenged as they are facing the toughest defense to date. Clemson has several defenders who could hear their named called on Day 1 of the NFL Draft. Will Heldt is a game changing defensive end and will test the Hokies tackles who have struggled at times this season. Sammy Brown has been the leader of the Tigers defense for a few years and will play a major role in shutting down the Hokies rushing attack. In my opinion, the best player on the Tigers roster is Ashton Hampton. He's a lockdown corner who has performed at an incredibly high level this season. Grunkemeyer will need to be prepared to fit the ball in tight windows if he plans on targeting Hampton. I believe Ethan Grunkemeyer is one of the best quarterbacks to ever dawn the orange and maroon and this is his prove it game against an incredible defense. I expect him to get the ball to Luke Reynolds and Que'Sean Brown early and often. Establish the star players and then let Jeffrey Overton Jr create explosive plays with his dynamic ability in open field. This will be a difficult test for the Hokies offense, but I believe Grunk can lead this team to victory. James Franklin gets his statement win and Virginia Tech beats the Tigers for the first time since 2007. Prediction: Virginia Tech 21 , Clemson 17 Haden Tolbert Virginia Tech heads into Death Valley Saturday night with a chance to make a statement. The Hokies have shown plenty of promise this season, especially through the air, but Clemson presents a completely different challenge on the road. Ethan Grunkemeyer and the passing game will be critical. If Virginia Tech can consistently move the ball and hit explosive plays, the Hokies have enough firepower to keep this game close. The biggest concern is the offensive line and the running game. Virginia Tech can't afford to become one-dimensional against Clemson's defensive front. If the Tigers can generate pressure and force Grunkemeyer into obvious passing situations, the Hokies could have a long night. Defensively, Virginia Tech's biggest priority should be forcing Clemson to throw. The Tigers haven't been especially productive through the air this season, so Brent Pry's defense needs to make Clemson prove it can win that way. Ultimately, I think this comes down to the fourth quarter. Virginia Tech has had opportunities to finish games this season, and Saturday will be another major test.
