On Saturday, they will welcome the Virginia Tech Hokies into Death Valley for a primetime kickoff. This will be the first time James Franklin has ever coached at Clemson . With this game featuring a pair of two-loss teams out of the ACC, expect for this game to play with our emotions for the entire 60 minutes or so. Clemson is 4-2 on the season and 2-1 in ACC play. The Tigers have wins over Georgia Southern, North Carolina, Cal, and Charleston Southern, but have suffered losses to LSU and Miami. Simply put, the Tigers have the record everyone probably expected them to have at the halfway point. As for Virginia Tech, the Hokies are 5-2 on the season, but have a propensity of giving up second-half leads . Here are the latest betting odds, how to watch, and a final score prediction of this game in question. Latest betting odds for Clemson Tigers vs. Virginia Tech Hokies According to the FanDuel Sportsbook , Clemson will be laying 2.5 points at home to visiting Virginia Tech. The associated moneylines for this game are Clemson -140 and Virginia Tech +116. This means you would need to wager $140 on Clemson to win $100. Conversely, if you were to place a $100 bet on Virginia Tech, you would pocket $116. The point spread suggests an incredibly close league game. The projected point total for this game comes in at a combined 49.5 points. If we were to factor in the 2.5-point spread, a potential final score for this game would be Clemson 26, Virginia Tech 23. With this game expected to be decided by less than a field goal, look for every possession to matter. Clemson Tigers vs. Virginia Tech Hokies game prediction Despite rarely playing each other all that much within the context of ACC play , we should be getting an incredibly compelling game in this one. Look for both teams to play well in all three phases. Clemson may have the edge on defense and special teams, but Virginia Tech arguably has the upper hand on the offensive side of the ball. Look for this tight game to be decided by only one possession. With it potentially being a chess match between Franklin and Tom Allen , this game might actually be won while Clemson is on offense and Virginia Tech is on defense. Because Clemson is the far more reliable team in the second half, look for Gideon Davidson to deliver the knockout punch on a well-orchestrated drive by Tait Reynolds. picks.blurb: Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the Hokies into Memorial Stadium, less than a year after he squared off against the Tigers in the Pinstripe Bowl at Yankee Stadium while playing for Penn State. In that game, Grunkemeyer threw for 260 yards and two touchdowns in Penn State's 22-10 win over Clemson. A third-year QB who committed to the Nittany Lions and James Franklin, Grunkemeyer followed his former Penn State coach to Blacksburg after Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech last November after the Nittany Lions parted ways with the 12-year skipper barely a month earlier. He has thrown for 1,984 yards and 15 touchdowns to two interceptions through seven games this season. Grunkemeyer and Virginia Tech lead the ACC in passing yards , though the Hokies have played one more game than Darian Mensah and the No. 1-ranked Miami Hurricanes. Clemson's passing game has been a complete contrast, to say the least. Through their first six contests, the Tigers have thrown a combined two touchdown psases between Week 1 starter Christopher Vizzina and former four-star freshman Tait Reynolds. The Tigers are second to last in the ACC in total offense with 340.7 yards per game while Virginia Tech ranks sixth (449.7) in the conference. Reynolds was 17 of 26 for 127 yards in Clemson's 37-0 win over Charleston Southern in Week 6. He has thrown for 943 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions entering his fifth start of 2026. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's prediction Oddsmakers have Clemson as a 2.5-point favorite over Virginia Tech, but as always, ESPN Analytics has its own odds for Saturday's game. ESPN's matchup predictor , which offers a prediction model based on its college football power index and other variables, gives Clemson a 55.9% chance to win. Virginia Tech has a 44.1% chance. The Tigers are No. 48 in ESPN's FPI with a 6.5 rating, which ranks 10th among ACC teams. Virginia Tech has a 6.6 rating that's one spot ahead of Clemson in ESPN's metrics. The Tigers are one spot ahead of Oregon State (6.0) in the FPI. Clemson football has longshot odds of reaching ACC title game entering Week 8 In ESPN's FPI entering Week 8, Clemson's chances of reaching six wins to qualify for a bowl game stand at 88.4%. The Tigers' chances of winning the ACC, however, are just 0.3%. That's down from 0.9% before the Tigers' 41-13 loss to the Miami Hurricanes on Oct. 3. Clemson's chances of reaching the 12-team College Football Playoff are 1.5%, which is down from 4.1% prior to the Miami loss and down from 22.2% entering the season. ACC football teams ranked by ESPN FPI: Who is best suited to beat Miami? There's a big gap between Miami and the rest of the ACC, but here is where Clemson and all 17 conference teams rank in ESPN's FPI: 17. Stanford Cardinal (-11.4 FPI) 16. FPI represents how many points above or below average a team is. Projected results are based on 20,000 simulations of the rest of the season using FPI, results to date, and the remaining schedule. Ratings and projections update daily. FPI data from seasons prior to 2019 may not be complete." picks.blurb: That's the mantra of Clemson coach Dabo Swinney . The Tigers (4-2, 2-1 ACC) host the Virginia Tech Hokies (5-2, 2-2) in a critical prime-time contest in Week 8 at Clemson Memorial Stadium. Clemson defeated Charleston Southern, 37-0, in Week 7 behind a defense that yielded 76 yards of offense and a rushing attack that produced 231 yards. Chris Johnson Jr. had two touchdowns, and Gideon Davidson led the Tigers' ground game with 59 yards on 13 carries. Tigers receivers hurt themselves with costly drops, which Swinney has repeatedly highlighted this week . Quarterback Tait Reynolds finished 17 of 26 for 127 passing yards in the true freshman's fourth start at quarterback. Virginia Tech is coming off a 34-24 win over Georgia Tech in Blacksburg. Hokies quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns in the win. He leads the ACC in passing yards: 1,984 through seven games. Hokies leading rusher Jeffrey Overton is averaging six yards per carry. Coach James Franklin's team ranks 28th nationally in total offense, which is good for sixth in the ACC. The Hokies are 32nd nationally in total defense, fifth-best in the conference. Clemson is 110th nationally in total offense with 340.7 yards per game, which is second to last among ACC teams ahead of only North Carolina. The Tigers are 46th nationally in total defense, which ranks 10th in the ACC. Will Clemson football beat Virginia Tech? ESPN's final score prediction Ahead of Clemson-Virginia Tech, ESPN's Bill Connelly predicted the final score using his popular SP+ metrics . Connelly has the Hokies winning by three points, which goes against oddsmakers' 2.5 spread favoring the Tigers. Connelly's final score prediction: Virginia Tech 26, Clemson 23. He gives the Hokies a win probability of 56%. Where Clemson football sits in ESPN SP+ rankings entering Week 8 Clemson is No. 56 in the ESPN SP+ team rankings , up five spots from last week. The Tigers have an overall rating of 4.0, up from 2.2 a week ago. Clemson is one spot below ACC rival Florida State (4.9) and one spot ahead of UCF in ESPN's team rankings. To break down Clemson's rating by unit, SP+ gives the Tigers a 23.1 rating on offense (No. 98 nationally, down one spot from last week) and a 19.5 rating on defense, which is 25th nationally and is up five spots from before the Tigers' win over Charleston Southern. In special teams, Clemson has a 0.3 rating, which ranks 20th in the nation. Virginia Tech is No. 40 in the SP+ team rankings with an overall rating of 8.9, one spot below the Oregon State Beavers and one spot ahead of the Baylor Bears. The metrics give the Hokies a 32.7 rating on offense that's No. 36 nationally, a 23.4 rating on defense that's No. 43 in the nation, and a minus-0.3 rating in special teams (No. 112). What are ESPN SP+ rankings? According to Connelly, SP+ is "simply a measure of the most sustainable and predictable aspects of football. If you're lucky or unimpressive in a win, your rating will probably fall. If you're strong and unlucky in a loss, it will probably rise." away.headline: Virginia Tech week 8 injury report: Latest updates ahead of Clemson matchup
away.blurb: BLACKSBURG — Following a win over Georgia Tech, Virginia Tech football heads out on the road to face Clemson in a pivotal ACC game. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Eleven players are on this week's report for Virginia Tech, the same as Week 6 against Cal and Week 7 against Georgia Tech. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: The Hokies' loss against Pitt came in spite of them racing out to an early 14-0 lead. The Panthers roared back with a 35-10 response, leading by as many as 11 in the final quarter. Though the Hokies mounted a nine-point rally, fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard game-deciding field goal was ruled no good. Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Georgia Tech: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Terry, Wright, Austin, Cunningham) Wide Receiver: 3 (Peterkin, Booker, Stuewe) Cornerback: 2 (Williams, Chadwick) Following its first 4-0 start since the 2017 season with wins over VMI , Old Dominion , Maryland , and Boston College , Virginia Tech (5-2, 2-2 ACC) lost back-to-back clashes with Pitt and Cal. Both were by one score, marking the first time since September 2024 that the Hokies have lost back-to-back games by seven points or fewer. The following week, Virginia Tech lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley. The Hokies held a 14-13 lead entering the final quarter, allowing the Golden Bears to pull ahead. Virginia Tech scored a go-ahead touchdown with 1:15 to go, but Cal's six-play, 75-yard drive — aided by a pair of penalty calls for roughing the passer (Kaleb Spencer) and defensive pass interference (Kenny Woseley Jr.) — enabled it to score the game-winning touchdown with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech marched the ball down to Cal's 7-yard line with three seconds remaining, but quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer's last-gasp throw to a contested Luke Reynolds was incomplete. The Hokies bounced back last week, though, with a 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech in Lane Stadium. Virginia Tech held a 24-3 lead at intermission and despite being outscored by 11 in the second half, it held firm. Grunkemeyer threw for 215 yards in the first half, though he only logged 35 more passing yards over the final two quarters. This year, Grunkemeyer's completed 72.9% of his passes for 1,984 yards (No. 4 in FBS), 15 touchdowns and two interceptions. There will be four reports in total: today's report, one report on Thursday and Friday, plus a game-day report two hours before Virginia Tech's tussle with Clemson. The Hokies' contest against the Tigers is set for Saturday, Oct. 24, at 7 p.m. ET in Clemso

away.blurb: Clemson football's initial availability report carries 10 injuries, one being fresh. Freshman wide receiver Gordon Sellars III is the only newly announced absence ahead of Saturday night’s game against Virginia Tech, while most of the remaining names have been unavailable for weeks. Sellars suffered a concussion and entered protocol following what Dabo Swinney described as the freshman’s best practice of the season. Clemson will hold him out when the Tigers host the Hokies at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN. The 6-foot-3, 200-pound receiver had finally worked his way back from the hamstring issue that limited him during fall camp. Swinney said Sellars made two impressive catches during practice and had established himself as Clemson’s fourth receiver behind Bryant Wesco Jr., Tyler Brown and T.J. Moore. Virginia Tech has its own problems up front. Offensive lineman Justin Terry is out, while Nathaniel Wright, Lucas Austin, and Montavious Cunningham are questionable. The Hokies allowed seven sacks in last week’s 34-24 victory over Georgia Tech . This article originally appeared on Clemson Wire: ACC injury report for Clemson vs. Virginia Tech: Who is out? Sellars has only three catches for eight yards this season, so Clemson is not losing a premium part of its passing game. His absence still shortens a receiver rotation that is already missing Cole Turner and reserve Chase Byrd. Turner has been away from the program since fall camp while handling a personal matter There is some good health news from the report. Running back Jay Haynes returned against Charleston Southern for his first game action since suffering multiple knee injuries in the 2024 ACC Championship Game. Defensive tackle Kourtney Kelly also made his Clemson debut after tearing his ACL during spring practice. away.headline: Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets?
away.blurb: The Yellow Jackets are going to be trying to pull off an upset against the Hokies today, but they are going to have to do so with some key players out. The final availability report is out for this game, and it includes the final status for running back Justice Haynes, who was listed as doubtful coming into Saturday, as well as offensive lineman Josh Petty and defensive lineman Landen Marshall. RB Justice Haynes and OT Josh Petty are going to be game-time decisions. If Haynes is unable to go today, Trelain Maddox and Chad Alexander would be the top options in the backfield for the Yellow Jackets today against Virginia Tech. Maddox is coming off the best game of his career last week against Duke. Riggs, the Yellow Jackets starting center, came back from an injury last week in the win over Duke, but was hurt during the game and did not return. He was not on the injury report this week and should be starting in the middle of the Yellow Jackets offensive line against what has been one of the ACC's best defensive fronts through the first part of the season. This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/georgiatech as Final Injury Report for Georgia Tech vs Virginia Tech: Who's in and Who's out for the Yellow Jackets? . Kickoff time is getting closer for Georgia Tech and Virginia Tech. How do these injuries impact Georgia Tech today? There are two notable names not on the injury report this week and those are Jameson Riggs and Noah Carter. Carter has been perhaps the Yellow Jackets' most consistent pass rusher (although the pass rush has not been very good), and without Walker, Boyd, or Hoffler to get after the quarterback, Carter is going to be relied on to put pressure on Hokies QB Ethan Grunkemeyer, and Virginia Tech's offensive line has not been one of the best in the ACC so far this season. As poorly as the season started for Georgia Tech, a win on the road against the Hokies would be something that could potentially start to turn their season around. The Yellow Jackets have only one conference loss and with the ACC looking wide open after Miami, Georgia Tech can star to build some momentum that could get them to their fourth consecutive bowl appearance under Brent Key. Trent Pearman and Bradley entered, respectively, after Clemson pulled starter Tait Reynolds with the game well in hand. "I asked him. I said, 'Do you want to go in, or do you want to put Brock in?' And he's like, 'Let's put Brock in,'" Swinney said. "So that was really his call. Coach C.V." home.headline: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out
home.blurb: Virginia Tech Football News: Key injury updates ahead of Clemson showdown, another sell out Skip to main content About One talking point going into the game, and really a talking point each week, is injuries and how they are going to affect depth charts for both teams. On Wednesday, the initial injury report for the game was released, and Virginia Tech cornerback Cam Chadwick was listed as questionable. On Thursday, another name was dropped, and the UConn transfer was off the list, which is a good sign. However, a couple of names still popped up for the Hokies who sound like they'll be game-time decisions at best. Offensive lineman Montavious Cunningham and cornerback Thomas Williams were both listed as questionable. As far as Clemson goes, defensive tackle Vic Burley is listed as questionable. When Franklin was hired by Virginia Tech, you knew that attendance at games was not going to be an issue with the Hokies' fans. Heck, they came out in droves last season, with a dismal season that saw Brent Pry fired after a Week 3 loss at home to Old Dominion. There are still two more home games remaining on the slate for Franklin and his team this season, and it was announced that those two final games will be played in front of a full house. The game on Nov. 14 against Stanford was already sold out, but now Virginia Tech has officially sold out the Commonwealth Clash against Virginia on Nov. 28. To think, Virginia Tech didn't even need to have two-for-one promos to get it sold out in late November. This is expected to be one of the better Commonwealth Clashes in some time. Virginia Tech Football Recruiting Virginia Tech All-Time Football Lists Virginia Tech Basketball Recruiting Virginia Tech Women's Basketball Coming off a 34-24 victory at home over Georgia Tech last Saturday, the Virginia Tech football team will hit the road for the first of two road games sandwiched around their bye week on Oct. 31 in Death Valley in South Carolina against Clemson. The Hokies will be looking to become bowl-eligible with a win after winning five of their first seven games, while the Tigers come in at 4-2 in a battle in primetime on ESPN between a pair of two-loss ACC teams in late October. NEW AVAILABILITY REPORT Cam Chadwick is off the report for the Hokies, while DT Vic Burley has been added for Clemson. pic.twitter.com/yEN9gsML54 Freshman Benjamin Eziuka played nearly 50 snaps against the Yellow Jackets last weekend and will be ready to go this weekend if Cunningham can't go again. It'll be a tough environment for Eziuka to play at Clemson, but Franklin doesn't appear to be nervous about putting him in. "He's dense; he's powerful in the weight room, and he's super trustworthy," Franklin said at his Wednesday media availability . "Obviously, everybody uses that quote: 'Do your job.' He's that guy. You know what you're going to get from him every single day." Virginia Tech announces Commonwealth Clash sellout This weekend's ACC slate begins on Friday

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Texas is looking to end a two-game skid and get its College Football Playoff hopes back on track against an Ole Miss team coming off its best performance of the year so far Getty Images Arch Manning grew up with Ole Miss all around him. His uncle Eli's jersey was retired in Oxford, and so was his grandfather Archie's No. 18. On Saturday night, Arch faces the Rebels for the first time, possibly at the lowest point of his career. Questions have swirled around Arch during a two-game losing streak that has the Longhorns on the brink of falling completely out of the polls after rising to No. 1 in September with a comeback win against top-ranked Ohio State . He threw two interceptions, including a pick-six, in the loss to Oklahoma , and last week he lost a fumble on a strip sack with two minutes remaining, allowing Florida to hold on for a win, Manning's first home loss as a starter. Afterward, Sarkisian said he would evaluate the offense, including Manning's role in the offense. Now Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) is trying to avoid joining 1965 Texas and 1957 Texas A&M as the only teams to lose three straight games in a season after entering as the AP No. 1 team. The Longhorns will be without the nation's sacks leader, Colin Simmons , who has a high ankle sprain. No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1, 3-1) has won two straight by a combined 63 points and has redisovered its groove following a 28-point win against nationally-ranked Missouri last week. Ole Miss vs. Texas: Need to know Arch Manning's evaluation : Manning is expected to start Saturday, but how short will the leash be? Backup KJ Lacey has gotten more first-team reps over the last two weeks, fueling speculation he could step in against the Rebels. Manning threw only seven interceptions in 13 games last season. He's up to five picks through six starts this season. "He's our starter, but I need to see a better version of Arch Manning like I need to see a better version of a lot of guys on our offensive football team right now, but we need to see a better version of him this week," Sarkisian said. Life without Colin Simmons : Simmons leads the FBS with 10.5 sacks and 16 tackles for loss. He had eight tackles, four TFL and a sack against Florida before he was carted off in the fourth quarter, and reports have him out three to four weeks. That's a problem against Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss , who has thrown a touchdown pass in 19 straight games, tied for the second-longest streak in Ole Miss history. His 20 total touchdowns rank second in the SEC, and Ole Miss leads the FBS in red zone touchdown percentage (87.5%). Ole Miss rebuilt itself after Florida : The Rebels left Gainesville in September after a 52-28 loss Golding called an "old-fashioned butt whooping." The Gators ran for 302 yards, and Ole Miss managed one tackle for loss and no sacks. Since a bye week, Ole Miss beat Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 at home. Kewan Lacy (122 yards) and Makhi Frazier (101) both topped 100 yards against the Tigers. The road remains the question. Ole Miss is 1-10 in its last 11 road games against ranked SEC teams, and Golding's lone road game as head coach against a ranked opponent was the loss at No. 21 Florida. Kewan Lacy comes home : Lacy grew up in Dallas as a Texas fan, and dreamed of playing for the Longhorns, but they never offered the running back a scholarship. "I can't wait to see them," Lacy said this offseason. He has 29 career rushing touchdowns, third in school history and the most in the SEC since 2025, though Golding has managed his workload since he missed the Florida game. His 13-game rushing touchdown streak ended against Missouri, but he still ran for a season-high 122 yards. Where to watch Ole Miss vs. Texas live Date : Saturday, Oct. 24 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium -- Austin, Texas TV : ABC | Live stream : Fubo ( try free ) Ole Miss vs. Texas: prediction, picks Texas is a 2.5-point favorite, and the SportsLine model projects a 29-17 Longhorns win. History backs it. Ole Miss is 1-6 straight up and against the spread as a road underdog against ranked teams since 2020, and Texas has won three straight home games against top-10 opponents. But is this the same Texas team that has been so successful at home? The Longhorns scored 17 points against a Florida defense that ranked last in the SEC, and the Gators sacked Manning five times with 11 tackles for loss. Texas hasn't scored more than 24 points against a power opponent. The offensive line is a mess, ranking 111th in sacks allowed, and the running game is subpar at 101st. The Longhorns are also 1-5 against the spread this season and haven't covered five straight. Ole Miss has the better quarterback and a run game that just went for 257 yards. Without Simmons, Texas loses the one defender built to wreck Chambliss' night. Texas also lacks championship-level coaching. picks.headline: Ole Miss on SI staff predictions: No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas
picks.blurb: No. 7 Ole Miss will take on its fifth-ranked opponent of the season when it travels to Austin to meet No. 19 Texas in Week 8. The Rebels picked up a critical win against Missouri in dominant fashion, while Texas picked up its second-straight loss in Week 7. Texas is playing with its back against the wall and is in a ‘must-win’ spot. Ole Miss desperately wants to avoid the position the Longhorns are currently in, considering the Rebels’ path the rest of the way. Going into the weekend, Ole Miss’ strength of schedule is No. 12 and its strength of record is No. 9 in the country, according to ESPN’s FPI. A win on Saturday would go a long way for the Rebels’ resume and they aren't taking the struggling Longhorns lightly either. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Longhorns is set for 6:30 p.m. CT on ABC. Ole Miss enters the weekend as 3.5-point underdogs. Ahead of the Rebels' latest top-25 matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Going into the year, and after the first three weeks of the season, Week 8 was a game I was fairly confident penciling in a loss for Ole Miss. However, now we’re actually here. With the new developments for each side throughout the month of October heading into this weekend, I like Ole Miss to get the job done in one of the country’s hardest atmospheres. Not to mention Texas won’t have some of its best players available, including Colin Simmons. He’s the type of player that’s a true game-wrecker and likely a top-10 pick in this spring’s NFL Draft. Considering Ole Miss is expected to start a true sophomore still gaining valuable experience at right tackle and a banged up Terez Davis at left tackle, there’s no telling how much of an impact Simmons could’ve had on the outcome of Saturday’s game. Though encouraging, Ole Miss’ performance running the ball and defending the run against Vanderbilt didn’t convince me that the Rebels were going to turn it around in those two aspects in a snap of a finger. That said, its dominant performance against Missouri did. Both games, particularly against the Tigers last week, were necessary confidence boosters for Ole Miss going into this weekend. Arch Manning appears to be pressing and Texas as a whole is in a make-or-break moment. It won’t be easy as the Rebels will certainly get the kitchen sink thrown at them by Texas, but I think Ole Miss pulls out another tight one. Ole Miss 30, Texas 24 Matt Galatzan This is pretty simple. If the Texas offense doesn't show up, Ole Miss is going to win by multiple scores. The Longhorns have an immeasurable amount of talent on that side of the ball, but the process, the protection and the quarterback have all been a disaster over the last few weeks. The Texas defense can keep them in this one, but it is all going to fall on the shoulders of Steve Sarkisian, Arch Manning, and the offense. Give me the better quarterback, and the better running game. Ole Miss 31, Texas 28 This is the most difficult prediction of the season so far for me. Texas has its back against the wall and really needs to win this game to keep its College Football Playoff hopes going strong. Ole Miss can afford one loss, but would not like to be in Texas’ current position on Nov. 7 when Georgia comes to Oxford. Logically, I want to pick Ole Miss because of the combination of the faith I have in the tandem of Trinidad Chambliss and Kewan Lacy, Texas having key players like Colin Simmons and likely Hollywood Smothers out with injuries. Also, Ole Miss’ defense seems to be peaking coming off a 31-3 win over Missouri. However, my gut just won’t let me pick against a desperate Texas team in a sold-out home game on a Saturday night. Give me the Longhorns to bounce back from two straight losses and beat Ole Miss in a close game. Texas 31, Ole Miss 28 Zion Trammell Ole Miss is coming off its best defensive performance of the season while Texas is struggling to find its offensive identity. The Longhorns have plenty of talent to succeed, which makes this matchup nerve-wracking. The Rebels have to grab an early lead and take the home crowd out of the game. I think Ole Miss will lean on Kewan Lacy and the Rebels will steal a huge road win. Cooper Ferguson I really do think that with the right system, Arch Manning can be a top-tier quarterback. He has the arm talent to compete with anyone in the nation, but the offensive line in front of him doesn't let him show it. Ole Miss wins through a defense that has grown increasingly strong over the past few weeks. For the first time in over a decade, Texas and Ole Miss meet on Saturday at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, Texas, at 7:30 p.m. ET (ABC). TOP PICK Who will win Ole Miss vs Texas: Texas -3.5 Archie Manning never played against Texas, but Arch Manning has the chance to lead the Longhorns to their first win against his grandfather and uncle's alma mater since 2012. It's a good time to buy low on a Texas team I would take to cover up to -5.5 at home against Ole Miss . Ole Miss vs Texas Over/Under pick: Over 53.5 While Texas' defensive advantage should make the difference in a Longhorns win, I'm expecting enough points to be scored for the Over to hit at 54.5 or better . The Ole Miss defense ranks 65th nationally in success rate (43.5%) and 89th in net EPA per drive, while allowing the most yards per game in the SEC (390). It's been at its worst away from home, allowing 35.6 points per game outside Oxford , helping the Over in all three of those games. But the Rebels have arguably the best QB in the country in Chambliss, who ranks top 20 in QBR (83.4) and TD passes (14). He and Kewan Lacy should move Ole Miss' offense with enough consistency for the Over to hit. I like Texas to win 31-24. A true must-win game is one that staves off elimination. Well, that's essentially what the Longhorns face Saturday night when Texas hosts the Ole Miss Rebels at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium. Just three weeks ago, the Longhorns were the No. 1 team in the nation. Now Texas is fighting for its College Football Playoff life. Steve Sarkisian has gone from the savior of the program to the hottest seat in America. And Arch Manning has gone from superstar to punchline. It has all gone so wrong so quickly. But Mississippi provides an opportunity for the entire Longhorns football program to put the past two weeks behind it and become the contender they're supposed to be ... on paper at least. We discussed after the Ohio State game that this Longhorns team might only play all-out and all-in when pushed the the brink . This is the brink. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas is staring down what seems to be a must-win vs. Ole Miss . The offense has given little reason for confidence and the defense, likely without Colin Simmons, has to contain one of the best QBs in the country. For Texas to end their losing streak streak, they'll need their most complete performance of the season. It's difficult for me to see them mustering that, especially against Chambliss, Lacy and the Rebels offensive attack. Final Score: Ole Miss 31, Texas 21 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction The Longhorns enter their matchup with Ole Miss this weekend on a two-game losing streak. Of late they have been plagued by sloppy play and injuries. Life won't get any easier against an Ole Miss team ranked seventh in the nation. The Longhorns have shown they have the talent to be an elite team but are now full of question marks. To beat the Rebels they will need to turn things around quickly but he last two weeks have not inspired alot of confidence. Final Score: Ole Miss 24, Texas 17 Trey Luerssen's Prediction I really don't know what to think of this team anymore. Could Texas rise from the ashes like a pheonix and play like the contender everyone thought the were? Or will the Longhorns lose three straight games and have one of the biggest falls any No. 1 team in the nation has ever had? Will UT figure out enough of its issues to play well and beat a playoff-calibre team in Ole Miss? Or will the entire Steve Sarkisian/Arch Manning era come crashing down on the DKR turf. The smart money is on the later. Texas and Manning has looked completely lost for two weeks. Desperation can be a great motivator. away.headline: Texas releases injury report for Ole Miss matchup
away.blurb: Texas star edge Colin Simmons is listed as doubtful for Saturday’s matchup after sustaining a high ankle sprain in the loss to Florida, while running back Hollywood Smothers is listed as questionable. Smothers reportedly missed practice on Monday due to a shoulder injury. Other names listed for the Longhorns are wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman (both questionable), as well as freshman edge Richard Wesley (out). Simmons going down during the Florida game is a huge blow for the Texas defense, as he has been playing at an extremely high level. Texas defensive coordinator Will Muschamp is going to need all hands on deck on Saturday to defend Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who has been one of the most dynamic playmakers in the country at the quarterback position, especially with the surprise news that Wesley is out. On top of that, Ole Miss will likely have star running back Kewan Lacy back on the field, as he is listed as probable on tonight’s injury report. The initial SEC injury report was released for the Saturday matchup between the No. 19 Texas Longhorns and against the No. 7 Ole Miss Rebels on Wednesday and while the Rebels have many more players on their side of the injury report, there are certainly some notable names for the Longhorns as well. Every game moving forward is a must-win for the Longhorns after dropping the last two matchups. They will need to get healthy moving forward as they try to navigate a difficult stretch in the schedule with eight straight games to close the season.

away.headline: Texas to face Ole Miss without nation’s leading sacker Colin Simmons
away.blurb: Texas will be without one of the nation's most disruptive defensive players Saturday when No. 19 Texas hosts No. 7 Ole Miss in Austin. Star edge rusher Colin Simmons has officially been ruled out, according to the latest SEC student-athlete availability report . The Longhorns could also be without their leading rusher, Hollywood Smothers, who was downgraded to doubtful. Meanwhile, Ole Miss received some encouraging news along its offensive line, but two starters remain questionable. Simmons' absence is arguably the most significant development for either team. The sophomore has accumulated 10.5 sacks, 16 tackles for loss and two forced fumbles through six games. He's responsible for more than half of Texas' 19 sacks this season and has been the centerpiece of one of the nation's most formidable defensive fronts. Even before leaving last week's 27-24 loss to Florida with an injury, Simmons had recorded eight tackles, four tackles for loss and the Longhorns' only sack. Fellow Texas edge rusher Richard Wesley has also been ruled out. Simmons' absence could provide a significant boost for Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, who will be facing a Texas defense allowing just 272.5 yards and 17.8 points per game. away.blurb: Ole Miss has some personnel questions heading into Saturday night's showdown at Texas, but one part of Wednesday's SEC availability report stood out more than anything else. Three starting offensive linemen appeared on it. Starting left tackle Terez Davis and center Brycen Sanders were listed as questionable, while right guard Patrick Kutas was listed as probable. The good news for Ole Miss is there's no reason to believe any of the three are in serious danger of missing the game. Kutas, especially, would be a surprise absence given his probable designation. Sanders returned to last week's 31-3 win over Missouri after leaving with an injury, and while Davis didn't come back, he remained on the sideline in uniform. Still, it's hard to ignore seeing three starters from the same position group show up on the report before a road trip to Austin. The concern isn't necessarily whether they'll play. It's the fact Ole Miss is entering one of its biggest games of the season with questions along the offensive front. As for Kewan Lacy, his inclusion feels far less significant. Lacy was listed as probable after briefly leaving last week's game with a hamstring issue, but he still ran for 122 yards against Missouri. At this point, it wouldn't be surprising if his name appears on most injury reports the rest of the season as Ole Miss manages the situation. The bigger story remains the offensive line. If the Rebels have all three starters available Saturday night, they'll likely feel good about where they stand. But heading into a hostile road environment against a talented Texas defense, it's a group worth monitoring. Colin Simmons' absence would be a big break for Ole Miss While Ole Miss is watching the health of its offensive line, Texas appears likely to be without one of the nation's premier pass rushers. EDGE Colin Simmons was listed as doubtful after suffering an ankle sprain in last week's loss to Florida. That designation aligns with reports earlier this week indicating Simmons is expected to miss multiple weeks. Barring a surprising turnaround, it would be unexpected to see him on the field Saturday. That's significant for Ole Miss. Simmons leads the nation with 10.5 sacks and has been the centerpiece of the Texas pass rush. The Longhorns also listed EDGE Richard Wesley as out, further impacting their depth up front. Texas still has plenty of defensive talent, so this isn't a matchup-changing development by itself. But for an Ole Miss offensive line dealing with multiple injury concerns, potentially avoiding the nation's leading sacker is about as favorable a piece of injury news as the Rebels could have received this week. picks.blurb: Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt defense preview: Kentucky offense can dominate Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 4:14 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will host Vanderbilt under the lights at Kroger Field on Saturday night, as it is the final game before the Wildcats enter a much needed bye week. The first College Football Playoff rankings will happen in two weeks after the Wildcats bye week, and there is a great chance we see Kentucky on the graphic if they can improve to 7-1 against Vanderbilt. There shouldn't be any extra motivation needed, as a lot of these players remember the beatdown that happened in Nashville last season when Vanderbilt defeated Kentucky 45-17 in a blowout fashion. Kentucky has an opportunity to return the favor on Saturday, as the Commodores have one of the worst defenses in the SEC. Vanderbilt is struggling in a lot of ways on the defensive side of the football, and Kentucky's offense should be able to capitalize. The Commodores rank last in the SEC in pressure rate and tackle for loss rate, they have had a difficult time of forcing negative plays. Vanderbilt also allows the highest success rate in conference, and Kentucky ranks fourth in the SEC in offensive success rate. The real key to watch in my opinion is early down conversion rate and third down conversion rate, Vanderbilt's defense allows the highest percentage to opponents in the SEC; Kentucky's offense is one of the best in the country at converting on early downs and they have a chance to improve on third downs this weekend. There are a few players to watch on Vanderbilt's defense, and we will get more into that when we release our X factors for the game. It starts up front with veteran edge defender Miles Capers and defensive tackle Issa Ouattara who is a massive 6'7, 305-pound lineman that clogs up the middle. On the back end, senior safety CJ Heard is a player who plays in the box and can make plays all over the field; Heard is dangerous as a blitzer, he is a sure tackler and is probably the best player on the team in coverage. However, there is a stark contrast in this defense compared to the one the Wildcats just faced in Oklahoma. Vanderbilt has allowed 121 total points in their last three games against Georgia, Ole Miss and Arkansas. The Commodores are allowing 40 points per game over the last three weeks. This is probably the worst defense left on Kentucky's schedule. This creates a perfect opportunity for the Wildcats to get things going offensively to improve to 7-1 heading into the bye week. Vanderbilt has the lowest pressure and tackle for loss rate in the SEC, as previously mentioned, so this is a game where all eyes are on the Kentucky offensive line. This is a game they should dominate, they can get movement in the running game and keep Minchey clean for 60 minutes. Vanderbilt is allowing over four yards per carry and 146 rushing yards per game. You have to wonder if the coaching staff keeps CJ Baxter out of this game to get him to the bye week so he is as close to 100% as possible for the final stretch; this could be another heavy Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes game. Kentucky has yet to put together four quarters of football where they are firing on all cylinders. I think this is the game we could see that play out, specifically from an offensive standpoint. Now that the Wildcats are in the thick of the College Football Playoff hunt, how you win in these games can matter to a degree. Kentucky needs a dominant win on Saturday to keep that momentum going into the bye week. picks.headline: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches
picks.blurb: Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Story by Wildcats Wire Vanderbilt offense preview: Kentucky can win in trenches Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 21, 2026 at 6:38 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football will try to keep to momentum rolling as they enter their bye week after they host Vanderbilt under the lights on Saturday. Kentucky just played one of the best defenses in the SEC in Oklahoma , and now they get to play one of the worst as we previewed the Vanderbilt defense . On the offensive side of the football, the Commodores are led by five star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The offense has struggled but Curtis has shown plenty of flashes although he has a ton of room to grow. In our Vanderbilt defensive preview, we really centered it around Kentucky's offense and how they can exploit the Commodores defense. We are going to do the same here because this game is about Kentucky staying focused to enter the bye week with a 7-1 record. Jared Curtis has a rocket for an arm and is a big, physical runner. Kentucky head coach Will Stein said that Curtis plays like Josh Allen, but he made it clear he was not making the comparison. Coach Stein is correct though, Curtis can make unreal throws down the field and runs with physicality that is rare at the quarterback position. However, Curtis has a long way to become the dangerous player he is capable of. Curtis still needs to fix little things like footwork, staying in the pocket and taking care of the football. Curtis has one of the highest turnover worthy play percentages in the SEC, he will put the ball in harms way against this Kentucky defense that has been incredibly opportunistic this season. Curtis does not have much help around him, his offensive line has struggled all season. Vanderbilt allows the highest pressure rate in the SEC, which has led to Curtis being sacked a total of 10 times this season. However, Curtis is really difficult to bring down with his 6'4, 230-pound frame. His ability to erase sack opportunities is similar to South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers. Kentucky will win this matchup in the trenches, this deep defensive line unit will be able to get consistent pressure on Curtis. The biggest question will be how often they can convert those pressures into sacks, which they have been better at doing the last two weeks against Sam Leavitt and John Mateer. It will be a vital coaching point all week for the Wildcats to finish the play and get Curtis on the ground. If they allow Curtis to extend plays with his legs and erase sacks, it can lead to big plays down field as a passer or scrambling for a first down. Luckily for Kentucky, they won't have to see wide receiver Tre Richardson as he transferred to Louisville. Richardson lit them up last year down the field with Diego Pavia throwing all over this defense. I am sure a lot of the returning Wildcats on the defense have not forgotten that 45-17 beatdown last year in Nashville. This motivation will play a factor against a Vanderbilt team that is in a rebuilding stage. The Commodores receiving room is led by veteran Junior Sherrill, who is far and away the best weapon on this offense. Sherrill leads Vanderbilt in receptions, yards and touchdowns. He has four touchdowns on the season and all other wide receivers have combined for just one on the season. This is the guy to watch when Vanderbilt is on offense, they will force feed him the football. Vanderbilt offensive coordinator Tim Beck has one of the most unique offenses in the country and we saw how dangerous it could be last season. However, they lost their quarterback Diego Pavia who thrived in his system, they also lost their mismatch tight end Eli Stowers and the explosive weapon Richardson who transferred to Louisville. This is very much a transition year for this offense and it shows up on film. Kentucky has another opportunity to make a statement on defense after creating four turnovers and holding Oklahoma to just one touchdown last week. Kentucky Football continues to climb in the AP Top 25 Poll , moving up three spots to No. 12 after defeating Oklahoma, 21-13, in Norman. The Wildcats improved to 6-1 overall, became bowl eligible, and strengthened their hopes of reaching the College Football Playoff in head coach Will Stein’s first season. The victory was far from perfect, as Kentucky’s offense struggled to find consistency after an impressive opening drive. However, the defense came up with several crucial plays down the stretch to help the Wildcats secure another impressive road win. Kentucky’s offense looked sharp on its opening possession, slicing through Oklahoma’s defense and setting the tone early. However, the unit stalled after that drive and did not score another offensive touchdown until 12:53 remained in the fourth quarter, when quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Willie Rodriguez for the Wildcats’ second touchdown of the game. Although the final score was relatively low, Kentucky’s defense also struggled at times in the first half. Safety Jordan Castell came up with a key interception when Oklahoma attempted a fake field goal in the first quarter, ending a promising Sooners possession. The Wildcats’ defense began to turn things around late in the third quarter when Ty Bryant intercepted Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer, giving Kentucky possession in Sooners territory. From there, the defense took control. Oklahoma recorded two three-and-outs and threw two more interceptions. Castell returned one for a pick-six, extending Kentucky’s lead to eight points, while Bryant secured the game-ending interception to seal the victory. While the game was sloppy on both sides, Kentucky found a way to finish strong. The Wildcats improved to 6-1, earned bowl eligibility, and continued building momentum as they pursue a potential College Football Playoff appearance. Now, Kentucky returns home to Kroger Field to face Vanderbilt, looking to avenge consecutive losses to the Commodores while losing three of four in the series. Kentucky fell 45-17 on the road last season after suffering a 20-13 defeat at home the year before. With Vanderbilt struggling through a disappointing season, the Wildcats will have an opportunity to extend their winning ways and continue climbing the national rankings. But if this last weekend showed us anything, it’s that upsets are commonplace this season, and Kentucky can’t afford to come out flat against a Commodores team starving for its first SEC win of the season. That, and Vandy did nearly pull off an upset over an Auburn team that just won at No. 1 Georgia. The Dores may be struggling, but they’ve still got an SEC roster. Vanderbilt Commodores (3-4, 0-4 in SEC) Vanderbilt has struggled through the first seven games of the season, and life after former quarterback Diego Pavia has been challenging. The Commodores finished the 2025 regular season with an impressive 10-2 record before losing to Iowa in the Citrus Bowl, ending the year at 10-3. However, the Dores have not come close to replicating that success this season. Vanderbilt suffered a disappointing 31-21 loss to Arkansas this past weekend. The Razorbacks entered the matchup on a 14-game Southeastern Conference losing streak, but they snapped that drought against the Commodores. One of Vanderbilt’s biggest challenges has been the development of 5-star true freshman quarterback Jared Curtis. The young signal-caller has shown flashes of his talent, but his inexperience has been evident. The drop-off from Pavia to Curtis has been noticeable, and Vanderbilt’s decision to start a true freshman at quarterback has come with growing pains. Through seven games, Curtis has completed 101/161 passes for 62.7%, totaling six passing touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has also been sacked 11 times. Curtis measures 6-foot-3 and weighs 230 pounds, giving him the physical tools to develop into a quality quarterback. He can also make plays with his legs, recording 55 carries for 144 rushing yards and two touchdowns. However, his turnover numbers and struggles under pressure will be areas Kentucky looks to exploit. Vanderbilt’s other major weakness has been its defense, particularly against the run. The Commodores have struggled to establish consistency along their front seven, which could create problems against Kentucky’s rushing attack. The Wildcats have a three-headed backfield featuring CJ Baxter, provided he is healthy enough to play, alongside Jason Patterson and Jovantae Barnes. If Kentucky can keep all three involved, Vanderbilt could have a difficult time slowing down the ground game. Kentucky’s offensive line, known as the Big Blue Wall, has also looked impressive this season. If the unit continues to open running lanes and control the line of scrimmage, the Wildcats could have a significant advantage. As for Vanderbilt’s offense, Curtis has several weapons at his disposal. Senior wide receiver Junior Sherrill has emerged as Curtis’ primary target. The 5-foot-11, 200-pound receiver has recorded 41 receptions for 628 yards and four touchdowns so far this season. Junior wide receiver Ja’Cory Thomas provides another option at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds. He has recorded 12 receptions for 195 yards and one touchdown. Vanderbilt also features junior tight end Jayvontay Conner, who stands 6-foot-4 and weighs 235 pounds. Conner has totaled 13 receptions for 146 yards, though he has yet to score a touchdown this season. Junior receiver Tristen Brown has added another option in the passing game, recording 12 receptions for 145 yards. In the backfield, Vanderbilt relies primarily on two running backs. Senior Sedrick Alexander, who stands 5-foot-9 and weighs 207 pounds, has recorded 61 carries for 270 yards and five touchdowns. Senior Makhilyn Young, at 5-foot-10 and 210 pounds, has added 52 carries for 216 yards and two touchdowns. For Vanderbilt to pull off the upset, Curtis will need to protect the football, make better decisions under pressure, and find ways to move the ball against Kentucky’s defense. The Commodores will also need to improve against the run to keep the Wildcats’ offense from controlling the game. Kentucky, meanwhile, will look to establish the run early, protect Minchey, and continue creating turnovers defensively. With the Wildcats playing at home and Vanderbilt struggling in SEC play, Kentucky has an opportunity to deliver another convincing win against a team that’s had its number. How to watch Kentucky Wildcats vs. Vanderbilt Commodores Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Time: 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 24 TV Info: SEC Network Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as an 11.5-point favorite. ESPN gives Kentucky an 85.4% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 6-1 and bowl eligible, with its attention now turning toward the College Football Playoff. Under first-year head coach Will Stein, the Wildcats have shown they can win in different ways, whether through explosive offensive performances or clutch defensive plays in lower-scoring games. Vanderbilt, meanwhile, is reeling after falling to 3-4 overall and 0-4 in SEC play. Losing to Arkansas after the Razorbacks had endured a 14-game conference losing streak raises further questions about the direction of the Commodores’ season. Kentucky also has extra motivation after losing to Vanderbilt in each of the past two seasons. With the Wildcats playing at home, an improving defense, and a rushing attack capable of taking control of the game, I expect Kentucky to avenge those losses and earn a convincing victory. away.blurb: Vanderbilt football heads out of town to Lexington, Kentucky this weekend to take on the No. 12 Kentucky Wildcats for its fifth SEC game. But before the game kicks off this weekend, we have to know who is going to be available Saturday night. Wednesday night, the SEC released its initial player availability reports leading up to this weekend’s slate of games. What was not know were the statuses of EDGE Brian Allen Jr., safety Dontae Carter and offensive lineman Mitchell Smith. On the first injury report, Allen Jr. is officially listed as out while Carter is listed as questionable and Smith is listed as probable. Tuesday, Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea announced that Allen Jr. did not practice due to an ankle injury, but Carter did practice wearing a no-contact jersey. In the case of Smith, Lea sounded hopeful Tuesday that he would be able to play after missing the last two games. In addition to those three, linebacker Josiah Broxton is doubtful for Saturday's game while safety Davin Chandler is listed as questionable. Along with Smith on the probable designation are cornerback Cayden Daniels and defensive lineman Hayden Bray. Vanderbilt’s initial injury report. Nearly half the league is down to its backup quarterback, whether due to injury or by choice. The only undefeated team in the conference is UCLA , while Oregon's conference title hopes are hanging on by a thread. Ohio State just picked up a huge win, but faces the prospect of being without Julian Sayin for the rest of the season. It's chaos, and when chaos is around, there's a chance someone unexpected will emerge and take advantage of it. So while No. 16 USC's trip to Madison this weekend to face Wisconsin might not be the headliner game of the weekend, it's a chance for two teams to step forward and stake a claim in the conference. USC has won two straight since dropping a game to Oregon, and perhaps most surprisingly, one of those wins has come on the road. The Trojans are 2-0 outside the Coliseum, which has been a serious problem for them during Lincoln Riley's tenure. Now they're back on the road facing a Wisconsin team coming off its first Big Ten loss at UCLA last week. The winner stays in the Big Ten title race with a chance to capitalize on the chaos. The loser will have to hope for a lot more chaos to befall the rest of the league going forward. USC vs. Wisconsin: Need to know Wisconsin has struggled with USC: They haven't shared a conference for long, but there is familiarity with these programs. Familiarity Wisconsin would sooner forget. USC is 7-1 all time against the Badgers, with the lone loss coming in the 2015 Holiday Bowl. They've only played once as Big Ten foes, and USC won that game 38-21 in Los Angeles during the 2024 season. As for the trip to Camp Randall, USC has won both the games in Madison, though the last meeting came in 1965. NCAA eligibility rules change every day, but I'm pretty sure none of the players who played in that game have remaining eligibility. Lincoln Riley is good off a bye: While Wisconsin was in Los Angeles losing to UCLA last week, USC was in Los Angeles chilling on the couch watching. That's typically been a good thing for the Trojans. Under Lincoln Riley, USC is 5-1 coming off a bye and has won three straight. Wisconsin has performed poorly in these spots of late: Wisconsin has played six home games against AP-ranked opponents under Luke Fickell. It has won only once in those six games. That win came last season against No. 24 Washington . As for the five losses, four of them have come by at least 14 points, though all four of them were against top-4 teams in the poll. If there was any time to wish for temperatures in the 40s with biting wind, it's when USC is coming to town. Instead, the forecast is calling for temperatures in the 60s with a manageable breeze. Still, even if the weather won't have an oversized impact, I like the under here. USC may have won its two road trips so far this season, but the offense didn't look great against Penn State , and this Wisconsin defense is good. I also don't have much faith in the Wisconsin offense. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Wisconsin's Huge Primetime Clash With No. 16 USC Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL Saturday night in Camp Randall Stadium could easily set the tone for the rest of the year for Wisconsin football. A win would instantly erase the pain from Week 7 out in Los Angeles, as it would represent Wisconsin's first victory over a legitimately good opponent and give head coach Luke Fickell another top-20 upset on his resume for the 2026 season, which would go a long way in helping him prove he's the man for the job in Madison. A loss, on the other hand, would even up the Badgers' Big Ten record at 2-2 and set them up with a must-win on Halloween in Iowa City, a situation nobody wants to be in. As Wisconsin continues prep for the Trojans , here's three bold predictions for the Saturday night showdown: Wisconsin shuts down star Trojans' tailback King Miller USC Trojans running back King Miller. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. All week long in the lead-up to UCLA, all we heard about was the Bruins' rugged ground game. A supposedly unstoppable force of nature, headlined by star ball-carrier Wayne Knight, was supposed to run rampant over the Badgers' front seven. Instead, Wisconsin held the Bruins to 44 rushing yards through the first three quarters (120 after a fourth quarter of mostly clock control from UCLA) while Knight himself posted just 23 yards on 13 carries. All told, UCLA averaged just 3.2 yards per carry. Surprisingly, that didn't matter because the Badgers couldn't contain Bruins' quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who completed 67% of his passes while tossing for 264 yards. But Wisconsin made a point; even the best rushing attacks in college football should expect to struggle against the Cardinal and White. USC has two very capable backs in King Miller (114 carries, 595 yards, four touchdowns) and Waymond Jordan (63 carries, 287 yards and two scores). However, the Trojans' ground game as a whole ranks just 77th nationally, one spot above the Badgers — both teams run for 152 yards per game. While USC's backs are capable, this isn't the most impressive rushing attack and Wisconsin just proved that it can make even the best ground games in the country struggle mightily. Miller has yet to run for fewer than 45 yards this season; I foresee that happening Saturday night. Colton Joseph takes care of the ball all night Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. After a rough three-interception outing in the upset win over then-No. 13 Penn State, Colton Joseph has taken care of the football, at least through the air. He's lost two fumbles, neither of which were recovered by the defense, but he's also gone two straight games without throwing an interception for the first time in his Badgers career. Against USC, there's no reason why he can't make it three. The Trojans have only intercepted three passes this fall across seven games; there's only 11 FBS programs that've played as many games and picked off fewer passes. Their pass defense as a whole has left plenty to be desired; USC is allowing 239 passing yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Joseph has also cut down on the "turnover-worthy plays," according to Pro Football Focus. After he combined for eight over the Badgers' first four games, he has just one over the last two games. The turnover battle is going to be huge in order to pull off an upset like this, but I think Joseph can keep it clean Saturday night. Wisconsin benches PJ Wilkins Wisconsin offensive lineman PJ Wilkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. Given how he's played, this wouldn't be a bold prediction under normal circumstances. But the Badgers have insisted on trotting him out there with the starters, and that was painfully clear in Pasadena when they moved Stylz Blackmon to center in place of the injured starter Austin Kawecki, despite the fact that Kawecki's backup Ryan Cory played well in his stead, which also forced Wilkins to start at right guard. At what point does Wisconsin give up on Wilkins as a starting-caliber offensive lineman this season? It's tried him at three spots — left tackle, right tackle and right guard — all of which have been problematic. He easily "leads" the team with 12 pressures, per Pro Football Focus, although having watched the all-22 tape I'd venture to say that's a generously low estimate. He just doesn't appear to have the quickness to hold up in pass protection. “It’s been a little bit difficult. When guys get dinged up, in particular Kawecki and moving Stylz back in there, we just felt like that was our best five," Fickell said this week . "We gotta find a way to make sure we have our best five up front every week.” Unfortunately, it's pretty clear the Badgers' "best five" doesn't include Wilkins at this point in time. With Kawecki probable as of the Wednesday injury report, he could return to center, meaning Blackmon could return to right guard. picks.headline: Behind enemy lines: USC expert previews Week 8 matchup at Wisconsin
picks.blurb: Behind enemy lines: USC expert previews Week 8 matchup at Wisconsin - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff F1 United States GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Williams, Bears hang on LeBron's biggest comeback Lendeborg shades Luka Canes' murky ACC future World Series preview Behind enemy lines: USC expert previews Week 8 matchup at Wisconsin Jordon Lawrenz, Badgers Wire Fri, October 23, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Wisconsin Badgers return to Madison on Saturday, Oct. 24, for a primetime showdown against No. 15 USC . USC is fresh off a bye week, while Wisconsin made the West Coast trip to UCLA, where they fell at the Rose Bowl, 17-7 . It was an embarrassing offensive performance for Luke Fickell's squad, yet somehow they hung in there against a team that has now cracked the top 10 in the US LBM Coaches Poll . With Week 7 rapidly approaching, Badgers Wire's Jordon Lawrenz had a chance to speak with Trojans Wire 's Matt Zemek ahead of the Big Ten matchup. Fresh off a bye week, do you think USC will be able to carry its momentum from the Washington and Penn State wins in Madison? The lesson of the Lincoln Riley era at USC is not to expect the Trojans to do anything the easy way. They did win at Penn State, which marks real improvement for a program that has consistently struggled to win Big Ten road games under Riley. However, that's a low bar. We can all see how mediocre Penn State is. The Nittany Lions lost to Michigan after losing to USC. The Trojans have a below-average defense, and so USC might be the get-right tonic for Wisconsin's offense. Should USC be favored? Probably, based on its eight-point win at Penn State. Does this mean the Trojans will get the job done? Hardly. This feels like a very close game, but whether USC wins or loses, don't expect the Trojans to have a smooth evening with no bumps in the road. It's not how they have historically operated on the road under Lincoln Riley. Who do you think the bye week benefited the most? Are there are any players who were banged up or are dealing with injuries? USC did need a week off. Not only does an off week give players a chance to rest, but in USC's case, the Trojans had played on seven consecutive weekends dating all the way back to August 29. When a team plays on that many consecutive weekends, it really needs a break. The key player USC is likely to get back for the Wisconsin game is tight end Mark Bowman. He has potential as a downfield pass catcher, but he is already a very good blocker who adds structure and balance to the USC offense. The Trojans were missing something when he was out the past few weeks. Trent Mosley is a more important player, but Bowman is right behind him in terms of value to USC's offense and quarterback Jayden Maiava. There are some defensive players who have a chance to get healthy during the off week, but the defense is a lot weaker than the offense. It's more important for the offense to be able to max out. That's where the off week can help USC more. What grade would you give Jayden Maiava through his first seven games this season? Jayden Maiava gets a B+. This might be a harsh grade, given that Maiava can't be blamed too much for the problems of the defense, but it remains that USC did not score 30 points against either Oregon or Washington. Maiava was solid against Oregon, but erratic against Washington. He has generally been very, very good. He played well at Penn State. However, for me to give an A to a USC quarterback requires that he rises to the moment in all the big games and all the defining situations a quarterback faces. He didn't do that against Oregon, so I have to limit him to a B+. I am holding him to a very high standard, because I think he's better than Dante Moore of Oregon and Arch Manning of Texas, among others. If he wants the highest possible grade, he will need to beat Ohio State or Indiana for sure. With Ohio State, Indiana, and UCLA on the schedule down the stretch, just how important is it to leave Camp Randall with a win? This is a must-win for Lincoln Riley with the brutal schedule ahead. USC will have a tough time beating Ohio State, Indiana, and UCLA. The Trojans have to finish 10-2 to make the playoff and convince everyone they are back where they belong in the college football world. Until they do that, they are an unproven team and a failed program. Beating Wisconsin is absolutely necessary to save Lincoln Riley's job. A loss here means USC could easily finish 8-4, which is nowhere near good enough for the program, the administration, and most of all, the fans. A loss here would have the pitchforks out for Riley. He would go into the Ohio State-Indiana gauntlet in huge trouble, and the roof could cave in on him. A loss to Wisconsin is an absolute and unmitigated disaster for the Trojans. In what areas do you believe USC has the edge over Wisconsin in this game? USC's main advantage is at quarterback. Maiava versus Colton Joseph is a mismatch. UCLA absolutely smothered Joseph and the rest of the Wisconsin offense. Maiava plays for Lincoln Riley, one of the best quarterback coaches in modern times, and has been above average on a consistent basis this season, the Washington game being the one primary exception. This is where USC has to create separation from Wisconsin. Maiava playing up to his standard, or even close to it, will give USC the clear upper hand. Wisconsin will need Maiava to have an off night in order to pull off the upset. Final score prediction? USC 27, Wisconsin 20. USC doesn't blow out Big Ten opponents on the road at night, but Wisconsin just isn't in a position to score enough to overcome a much more talented USC team. USC is one of eight Big Ten teams with only one conference loss – a stat that the Trojans will look to preserve for when the first College Football Playoff rankings of the year are released Nov. 3. A win against Wisconsin could give USC some wiggle room with tough opponents like No. 3 Ohio State, No. 6 Indiana and No. 9 UCLA still remaining on the slate. If USC loses this game, its chances of making the CFP will plummet. Who’s better? USC’s efficiency on offense should give it a considerable advantage, and the bye week should have the Trojans rested and revitalized. But Wisconsin has a few intangibles in its favor. They’re a hard-nosed, traditional Big Ten team with a home stadium that can be overwhelming. USC has been preparing for that all week by blaring House of Pain’s “Jump Around” through the practice facility and meeting rooms. Matchup to watch: Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph vs. USC’s run defense. Joseph isn’t overly efficient with his arm and is completing 54.7% of his passes, so he makes up for lost opportunities with his legs to the tune of 55.5 rushing yards per game. The Trojans' defense has already faced mobile quarterbacks this season, but keep in mind that this is also a defense that can start slow and is stronger in the second half. USC wins if: The offensive line will need to keep a high standard of protection , regardless of who is in the game. The trenches have shuffled around slightly and have still kept quarterback Jayden Maiava clean, allowing roughly one sack per game. The Trojans have to give Maiava enough time to make smart decisions against a defense that limits opponents to 171.2 passing yards a game. Prediction: USC 27, Wisconsin 17. The Lobos have since been on a tear, taking out New Mexico State, UTEP and Hawaii over the last three games on the way to a 5-1 overall run. New Mexico began their comeback with a TD in the third, then added two more trips to the end zone on the way to a 21-10 victory in the end. QB Toa Fa’avae was 5-of-10 for 59 yards and two picks. away.headline: Former USC TE could make season debut for Lobos against North Dakota State
away.blurb: Left tackle Cole Millward listed as questionable for Saturday's game New Mexico tight end Joey Olsen is listed as questionable for Saturday’s game against North Dakota State, per an availability report released by the Mountain West on Thursday. The 6-foot-5, 246-pound junior transferred to UNM in January after playing sparingly over two seasons at Southern California. He tore his ACL during offseason workouts and has been listed as out on every availability report but Thursday’s. Head coach Jason Eck first indicated that Olsen could potentially return this season in August, lauding the Lake Oswego, Oregon native’s work ethic in rehabbing his injury. “Joey, he’s going to keep stepping up … I do think he’s probably looking (to return) more near the end of this month,” Eck said on Oct. 5. “Maybe that Halloween game (against San Jose State) or something would be maybe his first thing, just getting enough months (removed) from his surgery that way.” If Olsen is able to return, he would provide UNM with another receiving option in a tight end room that’s been led by Cade Keith (15 catches for 212 yards, 2 touchdowns). Rated as a three-star prospect out of Lakeridge (Ore.) High School, Olsen caught 36 passes for 650 yards and 11 touchdowns as a senior to finish as the Pacers’ all-time receptions (119) and yards (2,303) leader. Offensive lineman Cole Millward is also listed as questionable for Saturday’s game. Eck said the 6-5, 297-pound senior tweaked his ankle early in UNM’s 21-10 win over Hawaii.
